content.label: Mixing Potions
content.text: A character might drink one potion while still under the effects of another or pour several potions into a single container. The strange ingredients used in creating potions can result in unpredictable interactions.

When a character mixes two potions together, roll on the Potion Miscibility table. If more than two are combined, roll again for each subsequent potion, combining the results. Unless the effects are immediately obvious, reveal them only when they become evident.

rows: Both potions lose their effects, and the mixture creates a magical explosion in a 5-foot-radius [Sphere](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/sphere) centered on itself. Each creature in that area takes 4d10 Force damage.
Both potions lose their effects, and the mixture becomes an ingested poison of your choice (see "Poison" in chapter 3).
Both potions work, but with their numerical effects and durations halved. If a potion has no numerical effect and no duration, it instead loses its effect.
Both potions work, but the numerical effects and duration of one potion are doubled. If neither potion has anything to double in this way, they work normally.

Only one potion works, but its effects are permanent. Choose the simplest effect to make permanent or the one that seems the most fun. For example, a *[Potion of Healing](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/potion-of-healing)* might increase the drinker's Hit Point maximum by 2d4 + 2, or a *[Potion of Invisibility](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/potion-of-invisibility)* might give the drinker the [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) condition indefinitely. At your discretion, a *[Dispel Magic](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/dispel-magic)* spell or similar magic might end this lasting effect.
content.title: Potion Miscibility

rows: Aligned. The item seeks to defeat or destroy those of a diametrically opposed alignment. Such an item is never Neutral.
Bane. The item seeks to thwart or destroy creatures of a particular type, such as Constructs, Fiends, or Undead.
Creator Seeker. The item seeks its creator and wants to understand why it was created.
Destiny Seeker. The item believes it and its bearer have key roles to play in future events.
Destroyer. The item craves destruction and goads its user to fight arbitrarily.
Glory Seeker. The item seeks renown as the greatest magic item in the world by winning fame or notoriety for its user.
Lore Seeker. The item craves knowledge or is determined to solve a mystery, learn a secret, or unravel a cryptic prophecy.
Protector. The item seeks to defend a particular kind of creature, such as elves or werewolves.
Soulmate Seeker. The item seeks another sentient magic item, perhaps one that is similar to itself.
Templar. The item seeks to defend the servants and interests of a particular deity.

If a creature of that type takes damage from the ammunition, the creature makes a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking an extra 6d10 Force damage on a failed save or half as much extra damage on a successful one.
After dealing its extra damage to a creature, the ammunition becomes nonmagical.
Your Constitution score is 19 while you wear this amulet. It has no effect on you if your Constitution is already 19 or higher without it.
While wearing this amulet, you can't be targeted by Divination spells or perceived through magical scrying sensors unless you allow it.

content.text: While wearing this amulet, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to name a location that you are familiar with on another plane of existence. Then make a DC 15 Intelligence ([Arcana](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/arcana)) check. On a successful check, you cast *[Plane Shift](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/plane-shift)*. On a failed check, you and each creature and object within 15 feet of you travel to a random destination determined by rolling 1d100 and consulting the following table.

content.text: While holding this Shield, you can take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to cause it to animate. The Shield leaps into the air and hovers in your space to protect you as if you were wielding it, leaving your hands free. The Shield remains animate for 1 minute, until you take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to end this effect, or until you die or have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition, at which point the Shield falls to the ground or into your hand if you have one free.

This item first appears to be a sealed iron barrel weighing 500 pounds. The barrel has a hidden catch, which can be found with a successful DC 20 Intelligence ([Investigation](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/investigation)) check. Releasing the catch unlocks a hatch at one end of the barrel, allowing two Medium or smaller creatures to crawl inside. Ten levers are set in a row at the far end, each in a neutral position, able to move up or down. When certain levers are used, the apparatus transforms to resemble a giant lobster.

The *Apparatus of the Crab* is a Large object with the following statistics: **AC** 20; **HP** 200; **Speed** 30 ft., Swim 30 ft. (or 0 ft. for both if the legs aren't extended); **Immunity** to Poison and Psychic damage.

To be used as a vehicle, the apparatus requires one pilot. While the apparatus's hatch is closed, the compartment is airtight and watertight. The compartment holds enough air for 10 hours of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.
The apparatus floats on water. It can also go underwater to a depth of 900 feet. Below that, the vehicle takes 2d6 Bludgeoning damage each minute from pressure.

A creature in the compartment can take a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to move as many as two of the apparatus's levers up or down. After each use, a lever goes back to its neutral position. Each lever, from left to right, functions as shown in the *Apparatus of the Crab* Levers table.

rows: Legs extend, allowing the apparatus to walk and swim.

Legs retract, reducing the apparatus's [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) and [Swim Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/swim-speed) to 0 and making it unable to benefit from bonuses to speed.
Side window shutters open (two per side).
Side window shutters close (two per side).
Two claws extend from the front side of the apparatus.
Each extended claw makes the following melee attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 7 (2d6) Bludgeoning damage.
Each extended claw makes the following melee attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* The target has the [Grappled](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/grappled) condition (escape DC 15).
The apparatus walks or swims forward provided its legs are extended.
The apparatus walks or swims backward provided its legs are extended.
The apparatus turns 90 degrees counterclockwise provided its legs are extended.
The apparatus turns 90 degrees clockwise provided its legs are extended.
Eyelike fixtures emit [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 30-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 30 feet.
The apparatus sinks up to 20 feet if it's in liquid.
The apparatus rises up to 20 feet if it's in liquid.
The rear hatch unseals and opens.
The rear hatch closes and seals.

content.label: Curse
content.text: This armor is cursed, a fact that is revealed only when the *Identify* spell is cast on the armor or you attune to it. Attuning to the armor curses you until you are targeted by a *Remove Curse* spell or similar magic; removing the armor fails to end the curse. content.text: You gain a +2 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) against ranged attack rolls while you wield this Shield. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC.
Whenever an attacker makes a ranged attack roll against a target within 5 feet of you, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to become the target of the attack instead.
This heavy cloth bag contains 3d4 dry beans when found. The bag weighs half a pound regardless of how many beans it contains and becomes a nonmagical item when it no longer contains any beans.

If you dump one or more beans out of the bag, they explode in a 10-foot-radius [Sphere](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/sphere) centered on them. All the dumped beans are destroyed in the explosion, and each creature in the [Sphere](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/sphere), including you, makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 5d4 Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

If you remove a bean from the bag, plant it in dirt or sand, and then water it, the bean disappears as it produces an effect 1 minute later from the ground where it was planted. The DM can choose an effect from the following table or determine it randomly.

rows: 5d4 toadstools sprout. If a creature eats a toadstool, roll any die. On an odd roll, the eater must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 5d6 Poison damage and have the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition for 1 hour. On an even roll, the eater gains 5d6 [Temporary Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points) for 1 hour.
A geyser erupts and spouts water, beer, mayonnaise, tea, vinegar, wine, or oil (DM's choice) 30 feet into the air for 1d4 minutes.
A [Treant](srd-5.2/14/treant/treant) sprouts. Roll any die. On an odd roll, the treant is Chaotic Evil. On an even roll, the treant is Chaotic Good.

An animate but immobile stone statue in your likeness rises and makes verbal threats against you. If you leave it and others come near, it describes you as the most heinous of villains and directs the newcomers to find and attack you. If you are on the same plane of existence as the statue, it knows where you are. The statue becomes inanimate after 24 hours.
A campfire with green flames springs forth and burns for 24 hours or until it is extinguished.

1d4 + 4 bright-pink toads crawl forth. Whenever a toad is touched, it transforms into a Large or smaller monster of the DM's choice that acts in accordance with its alignment and nature. The monster remains for 1 minute, then disappears in a puff of bright-pink smoke.
A hungry [Bulette](srd-5.2/14/bulettes/bulette) burrows up and attacks.
A fruit tree grows. It has 1d10 + 20 fruit, 1d8 of which act as randomly determined potions. The tree vanishes after 1 hour. Picked fruit remains, retaining any magic for 30 days.

A nest of 1d4 + 3 rainbow-colored eggs springs up. Any creature that eats an egg makes a DC 20 Constitution saving throw. On a successful save, a creature permanently increases its lowest ability score by 1, randomly choosing among equally low scores. On a failed save, the creature takes 10d6 Force damage from an internal explosion.

A pyramid with a 60-foot-square base bursts upward. Inside is a burial chamber containing a [Mummy](srd-5.2/14/mummies/mummy), a [Mummy Lord](srd-5.2/14/mummies/mummy-lord), or some other Undead of the DM's choice. Its sarcophagus contains treasure of the DM's choice.
A giant beanstalk sprouts, growing to a height of the DM's choice. The top leads where the DM chooses, such as to a great view, a cloud giant's castle, or another plane of existence.

content.text: This bag resembles a *[Bag of Holding](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/bag-of-holding)* but is a feeding orifice for a gigantic extradimensional creature. Turning the bag inside out closes the orifice.

The extradimensional creature attached to the bag can sense whatever is placed inside the bag. Animal or vegetable matter placed wholly in the bag is devoured and lost forever. When part of a living creature is placed in the bag, as happens when someone reaches inside it, there is a 50 percent chance that the creature is pulled inside the bag. A creature inside the bag can take an action to try to escape, doing so with a successful DC 15 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check. Another creature can take an action to reach into the bag to pull a creature out, doing so with a successful DC 20 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check, provided the puller isn't pulled inside the bag first. Any creature that starts its turn inside the bag is devoured, its body destroyed.

Inanimate objects can be stored in the bag, which can hold a cubic foot of such material. However, once each day, the bag swallows any objects inside it and spits them out into another plane of existence. The DM determines the time and plane.
If the bag is pierced or torn, it is destroyed, and anything contained within it is transported to a random location on the Astral Plane.

This bag has an interior space considerably larger than its outside dimensions—roughly 2 feet square and 4 feet deep on the inside. The bag can hold up to 500 pounds, not exceeding a volume of 64 cubic feet. The bag weighs 5 pounds, regardless of its contents. Retrieving an item from the bag requires a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action.

If the bag is overloaded, pierced, or torn, it is destroyed, and its contents are scattered in the Astral Plane. If the bag is turned inside out, its contents spill forth unharmed, but the bag must be put right before it can be used again. The bag holds enough air for 10 minutes of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.

Placing a *Bag of Holding* inside an extradimensional space created by a *[Handy Haversack](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/handy-haversack)*, *[Portable Hole](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/portable-hole)*, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within a 10-foot-radius [Sphere](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/sphere) centered on the gate is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way and can't be reopened.
This bag made from gray, rust, or tan cloth appears empty. Reaching inside the bag, however, reveals the presence of a small, fuzzy object.

You can take a Magic action to pull the fuzzy object from the bag and throw it up to 20 feet. When the object lands, it transforms into a creature you determine by rolling on the table that corresponds to the bag's color. See the System Reference Document for the creature's stat block. The creature vanishes at the next dawn or when it is reduced to 0 Hit Points.

The creature is Friendly to you and your allies, and it acts immediately after you on your Initiative count. You can take a Bonus Action to command how the creature moves and what action it takes on its next turn, such as attacking an enemy. In the absence of such orders, the creature acts in a fashion appropriate to its nature.
Once three fuzzy objects have been pulled from the bag, the bag can't be used again until the next dawn.
This small black sphere measures 3/4 of an inch in diameter and weighs an ounce. Typically, 1d4 + 4 Beads of Force are found together.

You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to throw the bead up to 60 feet. The bead explodes in a 10-foot-radius [Sphere](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/sphere) on impact and is destroyed. Each creature in the [Sphere](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/sphere) must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 5d4 Force damage. A sphere of transparent force then encloses the area for 1 minute. Any creature that failed the save and is completely within the area is trapped inside this sphere. Creatures that succeeded on the save or are partially within the area are pushed away from the center of the sphere until they are no longer inside it. Only breathable air can pass through the sphere's wall. No attack or other effect can pass through.

An enclosed creature can take a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to push against the sphere's wall, moving the sphere up to half the creature's [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed). The sphere can be picked up, and its magic causes it to weigh only 1 pound, regardless of the weight of creatures inside.
This flavorless, gelatinous bead dissolves on your tongue and provides as much nourishment as 1 day of Rations.
While wearing this belt, you gain the following benefits:

items.label: Dwarvish
items.text: You know Dwarvish.

items.label: Friend of Dwarvenkind
items.text: You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Charisma ([Persuasion](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/persuasion)) checks made to interact with dwarves and duergar.

items.label: Toughness
items.text: Your Constitution increases by 2, to a maximum of 20.
In addition, while attuned to the belt, you have a 50 percent chance each day at dawn of growing a full beard if you can grow one, or a thicker beard if you already have one.
If you aren't a dwarf or duergar, you gain the following additional benefits while wearing the belt:

items.label: Darkvision
items.text: You have [Darkvision](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkvision) with a range of 60 feet.

items.label: Resilience
items.text: You have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to Poison damage. You also have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws you make to avoid or end the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition.

content.text: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, while you are attuned to this weapon, your [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) maximum increases by 1 for each level you have attained.

content.label: Curse
content.text: This weapon is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the weapon, keeping it within reach at all times. You also have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on attack rolls with weapons other than this one.

Whenever another creature damages you while the weapon is in your possession, you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or go berserk. This berserk state ends when you start your turn and there are no creatures within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear.

While berserk, you regard the creature nearest to you that you can see or hear as your enemy. If there are multiple possible creatures, choose one at random. On each of your turns, you must move as close to the creature as possible and take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, targeting the creature. If you're unable to get close enough to the creature to attack it with the weapon, your turn ends after you've used up all your available movement. If the creature dies or can no longer be seen or heard by you, the next nearest creature that you can see or hear becomes your new target.

content.text: While you wear these boots, your steps make no sound, regardless of the surface you are moving across. You also have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Dexterity ([Stealth](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/stealth)) checks.
While you wear these boots, you can cast *[Levitate](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/levitate)* on yourself.

While you wear these boots, you can take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to click the boots' heels together. If you do, the boots double your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed), and any creature that makes an [Opportunity Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks) against you has [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on the attack roll. If you click your heels together again, you end the effect.
When you've used the boots' property for a total of 10 minutes, the magic ceases to function for you until you finish a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

While you wear these boots, your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) becomes 30 feet unless your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) is higher, and your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) isn't reduced by you carrying weight in excess of your carrying capacity or wearing Heavy Armor.
Once on each of your turns, you can jump up to 30 feet by spending only 10 feet of movement.
These furred boots are snug and feel warm. While wearing them, you gain the following benefits.

content.label: Cold Resistance
content.text: You have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to Cold damage and can tolerate temperatures of 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower without any additional protection.

content.label: Winter Strider
content.text: You ignore [Difficult Terrain](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/difficult-terrain) created by ice or snow.

While wearing these bracers, you have proficiency with the [Longbow](srd-5.2/06/weapons/longbow) and [Shortbow](srd-5.2/06/weapons/shortbow), and you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls made with such weapons.
While wearing these bracers, you gain a +2 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) if you are wearing no armor and using no [Shield](srd-5.2/06/armor/shield).

While wearing this brooch, you have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to Force damage, and you have [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to damage from the *[Magic Missile](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/magic-missile)* spell.

This wooden broom functions like a mundane broom until you stand astride it and take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to make it hover beneath you, at which time it can be ridden in the air. It has a [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed) of 50 feet. It can carry up to 400 pounds, but its [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed) becomes 30 feet while carrying over 200 pounds. The broom stops hovering when you land or when you're no longer riding it.

As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can send the broom to travel alone to a destination within 1 mile of you if you name the location and are familiar with it. The broom comes back to you when you take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action and use a command word if the broom is still within 1 mile of you.

This candle's magic is activated when the candle is lit, which requires a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action. After burning for 4 hours, the candle is destroyed. You can snuff it out early for use at a later time. Deduct the time it burned in increments of 1 minute from its total burn time.

While lit, the candle sheds [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) in a 30-foot radius. While you are within that light, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on [D20 Tests](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/d20-test). In addition, a Cleric or Druid in the light can cast level 1 spells they have prepared without expending spell slots.

Alternatively, when you light the candle for the first time, you can cast *[Gate](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/gate)* with it. Doing so destroys the candle. The portal created by the spell links to a particular Outer Plane chosen by the DM or determined by rolling on the following table.

This cape smells faintly of brimstone. While wearing it, you can use it to cast *[Dimension Door](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/dimension-door)* as a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

When you teleport with that spell, you leave behind a cloud of smoke. The space you left is [Lightly Obscured](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/lightly-obscured) by that smoke until the end of your next turn.

You can make this carpet hover and fly by taking a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action and using the carpet's command word. It moves according to your directions if you are within 30 feet of it.

Four sizes of *Carpet of Flying* exist. The DM chooses the size of a given carpet or determines it randomly by rolling on the following table. A carpet can carry up to twice the weight shown on the table, but its [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed) is halved if it carries more than its normal capacity.

This hollow metal tube measures about 1 foot long and weighs 1 pound. As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can strike the chime to cast *[Knock](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/knock)*. The spell's customary knocking sound is replaced by the clear, ringing tone of the chime, which is audible out to 300 feet. The chime can be used 10 times. After the tenth time, it cracks and becomes useless.
While wearing this circlet, you can cast *[Scorching Ray](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/scorching-ray)* with it (+5 to hit). The circlet can't cast this spell again until the next dawn.
This fine garment is made of black silk interwoven with faint, silvery threads. While wearing it, you gain the following benefits.

content.label: Poison Resistance
content.text: You have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to Poison damage.

content.label: Spider Climb
content.text: You have a [Climb Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/climb-speed) equal to your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) and can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and along ceilings, while leaving your hands free.

content.label: Spider Walk
content.text: You can't be caught in webs of any sort and can move through webs as if they were [Difficult Terrain](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/difficult-terrain).

content.label: Web
content.text: You can cast *[Web](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/web)* (save DC 13). The web created by the spell fills twice its normal area. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

While you wear this cloak, it magically projects an illusion that makes you appear to be standing in a place near your actual location, causing any creature to have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on attack rolls against you. If you take damage, the property ceases to function until the start of your next turn. This property is suppressed while your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) is 0.

While you wear this cloak, Wisdom ([Perception](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/perception)) checks made to perceive you have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage), and you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Dexterity ([Stealth](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/stealth)) checks.

This cloak has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the cloak, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to pull its hood over your head and expend 1 charge to give yourself the [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) condition for 1 hour. The effect ends early if you pull the hood down (no action required) or cease wearing the cloak.
You gain a +1 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) and saving throws while you wear this cloak.

While wearing this cloak, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Dexterity ([Stealth](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/stealth)) checks. In an area of [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) or [Darkness](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkness), you can grip the edges of the cloak and use it to gain a [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed) of 40 feet. If you ever fail to grip the cloak's edges while flying in this way, or if you are no longer in [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) or [Darkness](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkness), you lose this [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed).

While wearing the cloak in an area of [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) or [Darkness](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkness), you can cast *[Polymorph](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/polymorph)* on yourself, shape-shifting into a [Bat](srd-5.2/15/bat). While in that form, you retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. The cloak can't be used this way again until the next dawn.
While wearing this cloak, you can breathe underwater, and you have a [Swim Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/swim-speed) of 60 feet.
While touching this crystal orb, you can cast *Scrying* (save DC 17) with it.

content.label: Crystal Ball of Mind Reading (Legendary)
content.text: While touching this crystal orb, you can cast *Scrying* (save DC 17) with it. In addition, you can cast *Detect Thoughts* (save DC 17) targeting creatures you can see within 30 feet of the spell's sensor. You don't need to concentrate on this *Detect Thoughts* spell to maintain it during its duration, but it ends if the *Scrying* spell ends.

content.label: Crystal Ball of Telepathy (Legendary)
content.text: While touching this crystal orb, you can cast *Scrying* (save DC 17) with it. In addition, you can communicate telepathically with creatures you can see within 30 feet of the spell's sensor. You can also cast *Suggestion* (save DC 17) through the sensor on one of those creatures. You don't need to concentrate on this Suggestion to maintain it during its duration, but it ends if Scrying ends. You can't cast *Suggestion* in this way again until the next dawn.

content.label: Crystal Ball of True Seeing (Legendary)
content.text: While touching this crystal orb, you can cast *Scrying* (save DC 17) with it. In addition, you have Truesight with a range of 120 feet centered on the spell's sensor.

data.subtitle: Wondrous Item, Very Rare or Legendary (Requires Attunement)

content.text: This cube is about an inch across. Each face has a distinct marking on it. You can press one of those faces, expend the number of charges required for it, and thereby cast the spell associated with it (save DC 17), as shown in the *Cube of Force* Faces table.
The cube starts with 10 charges, and it regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn.

This cube is 3 inches across and radiates palpable magical energy. The six sides of the cube are each keyed to a different plane of existence, one of which is the Material Plane. The other sides are linked to planes determined by the DM.

The cube has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can expend 1 of the cube's charges to cast one of the following spells using the cube.

content.label: Gate
content.text: Pressing one side of the cube, you cast *[Gate](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/gate)*, opening a portal to the plane of existence keyed to that side.

content.label: Plane Shift
content.text: Pressing one side of the cube twice, you cast *[Plane Shift](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/plane-shift)*, transporting the targets to the plane of existence keyed to that side.

As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can place this 1-inch adamantine statuette on the ground and, using a command word, cause it to grow rapidly into a square adamantine tower. Repeating the command word causes the tower to revert to statuette form, which works only if the tower is empty. Each creature in the area where the tower appears is pushed to an unoccupied space outside but next to the tower. Objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried are also pushed clear of the tower.

The tower is 20 feet on a side and 30 feet high, with arrow slits on all sides and a battlement atop it. Its interior is divided into two floors, with a ladder, staircase, or ramp (your choice) connecting them. This ladder, staircase, or ramp ends at a trapdoor leading to the roof. When created, the tower has a single door at ground level on the side facing you. The door opens only at your command, which you can issue as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action). It is immune to the *[Knock](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/knock)* spell and similar magic.

[Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) prevents the tower from being tipped over. The roof, the door, and the walls each have AC 20; HP 100; [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage except that which is dealt by siege equipment; and [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to all other damage. Shrinking the tower back down to statuette form doesn't repair damage to the tower. Only a *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* spell can repair the tower (this use of the spell counts as replicating a spell of level 8 or lower). Each casting of Wish causes the tower to regain all its [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points).
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

You can take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to magically coat the blade with poison. The poison remains for 1 minute or until an attack using this weapon hits a creature. That creature must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 2d10 Poison damage and have the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition for 1 minute. The weapon can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

You can take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to toss this magic weapon into the air. When you do so, the weapon begins to hover, flies up to 30 feet, and attacks one creature of your choice within 5 feet of itself. The weapon uses your attack roll and adds your ability modifier to damage rolls.

While the weapon hovers, you can take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to cause it to fly up to 30 feet to another spot within 30 feet of you. As part of the same [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can cause the weapon to attack one creature within 5 feet of the weapon.

After the hovering weapon attacks for the fourth time, it flies back to you and tries to return to your hand. If you have no hand free, the weapon falls to the ground in your space. If the weapon has no unobstructed path to you, it moves as close to you as it can and then falls to the ground. It also ceases to hover if you grasp it or are more than 30 feet away from it.
This stoppered flask sloshes when shaken, as if it contains water. The decanter weighs 2 pounds.

You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to remove the stopper and issue one of three command words, whereupon an amount of fresh water or salt water (your choice) pours out of the flask. The water stops pouring out at the start of your next turn. Choose from the following command words:

items.label: Splash
items.text: The decanter produces 1 gallon of water.

items.label: Fountain
items.text: The decanter produces 5 gallons of water.

items.label: Geyser
items.text: The decanter produces 30 gallons of water that gushes forth in a [Line](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/line) 30 feet long and 1 foot wide. If you're holding the decanter, you can aim the geyser in one direction (no action required). One creature of your choice in the [Line](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/line) must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or take 1d4 Bludgeoning damage and have the [Prone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/prone) condition. Instead of a creature, you can target one object in the [Line](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/line) that isn't being worn or carried and that weighs no more than 200 pounds. The object is knocked over by the geyser.

content.text: This box contains a set of cards. A full deck has 34 cards: 32 depicting specific creatures and two with a mirrored surface. A deck found as treasure is usually missing 1d20 - 1 cards.

The magic of the deck functions only if its cards are drawn at random. You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to draw a card at random from the deck and throw it to the ground at a point within 30 feet of yourself. An illusion of a creature, determined by rolling on the *Deck of Illusions* table, forms over the thrown card and remains until dispelled. The illusory creature created by the card looks and behaves like a real creature of its kind, except that it can do no harm. While you are within 120 feet of the illusory creature and can see it, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to move it anywhere within 30 feet of its card.

Any physical interaction with the illusory creature reveals it to be false, because objects pass through it. A creature that takes a [Study](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/study) action to visually inspect the illusory creature identifies it as an illusion with a successful DC 15 Intelligence ([Investigation](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/investigation)) check. The illusion lasts until its card is moved or the illusion is dispelled (using a *[Dispel Magic](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/dispel-magic)* spell or a similar effect). When the illusion ends, the image on its card disappears, and that card can't be used again.

You can increase one of your ability scores by 2, to a maximum of 22, provided you also decrease another one of your ability scores by 2. You can't decrease an ability that has a score of 5 or lower. Alternatively, you can choose not to adjust your ability scores, in which case this card has no effect.

The next time you enter combat against one or more [Hostile](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hostile) creatures, you can select one of them as your foe when you roll [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative). If you reduce your foe to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) during that combat, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on [Death Saving Throws](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/death-saving-throw) for 1 year. If someone else reduces your chosen foe to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) or you don't choose a foe, this card has no effect.

You disappear and become entombed in a state of suspended animation in an extradimensional sphere. Everything you're wearing and carrying disappears with you except for Artifacts, which stay behind in the space you occupied when you disappeared. You remain imprisoned until you are found and removed from the sphere. You can't be located by any Divination magic, but a *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* spell can reveal the location of your prison. You draw no more cards.
The card's medusa-like visage curses you. You take a -2 penalty to saving throws while cursed in this way. Only a god or the magic of the Fates card can end this curse.

Reality's fabric unravels and spins anew, allowing you to avoid or erase one event as if it never happened. You can use the card's magic as soon as you draw the card or at any other time before you die.
A powerful devil becomes your enemy. The devil seeks your ruin and torments you, savoring your suffering before attempting to slay you. This enmity lasts until either you or the devil dies.

You have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on [D20 Tests](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/d20-test) for the next 72 hours. Draw another card; this draw doesn't count as one of your declared draws.
Twenty-five pieces of jewelry worth 2,000 GP each or fifty gems worth 1,000 GP each appear at your feet.

You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on [D20 Tests](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/d20-test) for the next 72 hours, or you can draw two additional cards beyond your declared draws.
A Rare or rarer magic weapon with which you are proficient appears on your person. The DM chooses the weapon.

You gain the service of a [Knight](srd-5.2/14/knights/knight), who magically appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 30 feet of yourself. The knight has the same alignment as you and serves you loyally until death, believing the two of you have been drawn together by fate. Work with your DM to create a name and backstory for this NPC. The DM can use a different stat block to represent the knight, as desired.
You gain the ability to cast *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* 1d3 times.
Permanently reduce your Intelligence or Wisdom by 1d4 + 1 (to a minimum score of 1). You can draw one additional card beyond your declared draws.

An NPC of the DM's choice becomes [Hostile](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hostile) toward you. You don't know the identity of this NPC until they or someone else reveals it. Nothing less than a *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* spell or divine intervention can end the NPC's hostility toward you.

All forms of wealth that you carry or own, other than magic items, are lost to you. Portable property vanishes. Businesses, buildings, and land you own are lost in a way that alters reality the least. If you have a Bastion (see the System Reference Document), it is destroyed by some calamity beyond your control. Any documentation that proves you should own something lost to this card also disappears.
At any time you choose within one year of drawing this card, you can ask a question in meditation and mentally receive a truthful answer to that question.

An [Avatar of Death](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/mysterious-deck/avatar-of-death) appears in an unoccupied space as close to you as possible. The avatar targets only you with its attacks, appearing as a ghostly skeleton clad in a tattered black robe and carrying a spectral scythe. The avatar disappears when it drops to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) or you die. If an ally of yours deals damage to the avatar, that ally summons another Avatar of Death. The new avatar appears in an unoccupied space as close to that ally as possible and targets only that ally with its attacks. You and your allies can each summon only one avatar as a consequence of this draw. A creature slain by an avatar can't be restored to life.
Increase one of your ability scores by 2, to a maximum of 24.
A magic item (chosen by the DM) appears on your person. In addition, you gain 10 [Temporary Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points) daily at dawn until you die.
Every magic item you wear or carry disintegrates. Artifacts in your possession vanish instead.

You gain proficiency and [Expertise](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/expertise) in your choice of [History](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/history), [Insight](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/insight), [Intimidation](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/intimidation), or [Persuasion](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/persuasion). In addition, you gain rightful ownership of a small keep somewhere in the world. However, the keep is currently home to one or more monsters, which must be cleared out before you can claim the keep as yours.

Your soul is drawn from your body and contained in an object in a place of the DM's choice. One or more powerful beings guard the place. While your soul is trapped in this way, your body is inert, ceases aging, and requires no food, air, or water. A *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* spell can't return your soul to your body, but the spell reveals the location of the object that holds your soul. You draw no more cards.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.text: The avatar makes a number of Reaping Scythe attacks equal to half the summoner's Proficiency Bonus (rounded up).

actions.name: Reaping Scythe
actions.text: *Melee Attack Roll:* Automatic hit, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 7 (1d8 + 3) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage.

data.hp: Half the HP maximum of its summoner
data.languages: All languages known to its summoner

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.text: The avatar can move through other creatures and objects as if they were [Difficult Terrain](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/difficult-terrain). It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

content.text: Usually found in a box or pouch, this deck contains a number of cards made of ivory or vellum. Most (75 percent) of these decks have thirteen cards, but some have twenty-two. Use the appropriate column of the *Mysterious Deck* table when randomly determining cards drawn from the deck.

Before you draw a card, you must declare how many cards you intend to draw and then draw them randomly. Any cards drawn in excess of this number have no effect. Otherwise, as soon as you draw a card from the deck, its magic takes effect. You must draw each card no more than 1 hour after the previous draw. If you fail to draw the chosen number, the remaining number of cards fly from the deck on their own and take effect all at once.

Once a card is drawn, it disappears. Unless the card is the Fool or Jester, the card reappears in the deck, making it possible to draw the same card twice. (Once the Fool or Jester has left the deck, reroll on the table if that card comes up again.)

Two of the cards in the *Mysterious Deck* can earn a character the enmity of another being. With the Flames card, the enmity is overt. The character should experience the devil's malevolent efforts on multiple occasions. Seeking out the fiend shouldn't be a simple task, and the adventurer should clash with the devil's allies and followers a few times before being able to confront the devil.

The first time you attack with the weapon on each of your turns, you can transfer some or all of the weapon's bonus to your [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class). For example, you could reduce the bonus to your attack rolls and damage rolls to +1 and gain a +2 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class). The adjusted bonuses remain in effect until the start of your next turn, although you must hold the weapon to gain a bonus to AC from it.

While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class), and you know Abyssal. In addition, the armor's clawed gauntlets allow your Unarmed Strikes to deal 1d8 Slashing damage instead of the usual Bludgeoning damage, and you gain a +1 bonus to the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes.

content.label: Curse
content.text: Once you don this cursed armor, you can't doff it unless you are targeted by a *[Remove Curse](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/remove-curse)* spell or similar magic. While wearing the armor, you have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on attack rolls against demons and on saving throws against their spells and special abilities.

content.text: You can take a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to place these shackles on a creature that has the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition. The shackles adjust to fit a creature of Small to Large size. The shackles prevent a creature bound by them from using any method of extradimensional movement, including teleportation or travel to a different plane of existence. They don't prevent the creature from passing through an interdimensional portal.

You and any creature you designate when you use the shackles can take a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to remove them. Once every 30 days, the bound creature can make a DC 30 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check. On a successful check, the creature breaks free and destroys the shackles.

*Dragon Scale Mail* is made of the scales of one kind of dragon. Sometimes dragons collect their cast-off scales and gift them. Other times, hunters carefully preserve the hide of a dead dragon. In either case, *Dragon Scale Mail* is highly valued.

While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class, you have Advantage on saving throws against the breath weapons of Dragons, and you have Resistance to one damage type determined by the kind of dragon that provided the scales (see the accompanying table).

Additionally, you can focus your senses as a Magic action to discern the distance and direction to the closest dragon within 30 miles of yourself that is of the same type as the armor. This action can't be used again until the next dawn.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
The weapon deals an extra 3d6 damage of the weapon's type if the target is a Dragon.

This powder resembles fine sand. There is enough of it for one use. When you take a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to throw the dust into the air, you and each creature and object within a 10-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) originating from you have the [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) condition for 2d4 minutes. The duration is the same for all subjects, and the dust is consumed when its magic takes effect. Immediately after an affected creature makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell, the [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) condition ends for that creature.

This small packet contains 1d6 + 4 pinches of dust. As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can sprinkle a pinch of the dust over water, turning up to a 15-foot [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube) of water into one marble-sized pellet, which floats or rests near where the dust was sprinkled. The pellet's weight is negligible. A creature can take a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to smash the pellet against a hard surface, causing the pellet to shatter and release the water the dust absorbed. Doing so destroys the pellet and ends its magic.

As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can sprinkle a pinch of the dust on an Elemental within 5 feet of yourself that is composed mostly of water (such as a [Water Elemental](srd-5.2/14/water-elemental/water-elemental) or a Water Weird). Such a creature exposed to a pinch of the dust makes a DC 13 Constitution saving throw, taking 10d6 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Found in a small container, this powder resembles *[Dust of Disappearance](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/dust-of-disappearance)*, and *[Identify](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/identify)* reveals it to be such. There is enough of it for one use.

As a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, you can throw the dust into the air, forcing yourself and every creature in a 30-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) originating from you to make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. Constructs, Elementals, Oozes, Plants, and Undead succeed on the save automatically.

On a failed save, a creature begins sneezing uncontrollably; it has the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition and is suffocating. The creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The effect also ends on any creature targeted by a *[Lesser Restoration](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/lesser-restoration)* spell.

While wearing this armor, you gain a +2 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class). In addition, if an effect moves you against your will along the ground, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to reduce the distance you are moved by up to 10 feet.

content.text: Long ago, in the Dragonlance setting, elves and humans waged a terrible war against chromatic dragons. When the world seemed doomed, the wizards of the Towers of High Sorcery came together and forged five Orbs of Dragonkind to help defeat the dragons. One orb was taken to each of the five towers, and there they were used to speed the war toward a victorious end. The wizards used the orbs to lure dragons to them, then destroyed the dragons with powerful magic.

As the Towers of High Sorcery fell in later ages, the orbs were destroyed or faded into legend, and only three are thought to survive. Their magic has been warped over the centuries. Their primary purpose of calling dragons still functions, but they also allow some measure of control over dragons.

Each orb contains the essence of an evil dragon, a presence that resents any attempt to coax magic from it. Those who try to wield an orb's magic but lack sufficient force of personality might find themselves under the orb's control.
An orb is an etched crystal globe about 10 inches in diameter. When used, it grows to about 20 inches in diameter, and mist swirls inside it.

While attuned to an orb, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to peer into the orb's depths. You must then make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw. On a successful save, you control the orb for as long as you remain attuned to it. On a failed save, the orb imposes the [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) condition on you for as long as you remain attuned to it.

While you are [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) by the orb, you can't voluntarily end your [Attunement](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attunement) to it, and the orb casts *[Suggestion](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/suggestion)* on you at will (save DC 18), urging you to work toward the evil ends it desires. The dragon essence within the orb might want many things: the annihilation of a particular society or organization, freedom from the orb, to spread suffering in the world, to advance the worship of a dragon deity, or something else the DM decides.

content.label: Random Properties
content.text: An *Dragon Orb* has the following random properties:

items.text: 2 minor beneficial properties
1 minor detrimental property
1 major detrimental property

content.label: Spells
content.text: The orb has 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 expended charges daily at dawn. If you control the orb, you can cast one of the spells on the following table from it. The table indicates how many charges you must expend to cast the spell.

content.label: Call Dragons
content.text: While you control the orb, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to cause the orb to issue a telepathic call that extends in all directions for 40 miles. Chromatic dragons in range feel compelled to come to the orb as soon as possible by the most direct route. Dragon deities are unaffected by this call. Chromatic dragons drawn to the orb might be [Hostile](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hostile) toward you for compelling them against their will. Once you have used this property, it can't be used again for 1 hour.

content.label: Destroying an Orb
content.text: An *Dragon Orb* has AC 20 and is destroyed if it takes damage from a +3 Weapon or a *[Disintegrate](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/disintegrate)* spell. Nothing else can harm it.

While this bowl is filled with water and you are within 5 feet of it, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to summon a [Water Elemental](srd-5.2/14/water-elemental/water-elemental). The elemental appears in an unoccupied space as close to the bowl as possible, understands your languages, obeys your commands, and takes its turn immediately after you on your [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) count. The elemental disappears after 1 hour, when it dies, or when you dismiss it as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action). The bowl can't be used this way again until the next dawn.
The bowl is about 1 foot in diameter and half as deep. It holds about 3 gallons.

While you are within 5 feet of this brazier, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to summon a [Fire Elemental](srd-5.2/14/fire-elemental/fire-elemental). The elemental appears in an unoccupied space as close to the brazier as possible, understands your languages, obeys your commands, and takes its turn immediately after you on your [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) count. The elemental disappears after 1 hour, when it dies, or when you dismiss it as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action). The brazier can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

While gently swinging this censer, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to summon an [Air Elemental](srd-5.2/14/air-elemental/air-elemental). The elemental appears in an unoccupied space as close to the censer as possible, understands your languages, obeys your commands, and takes its turn immediately after you on your [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) count. The elemental disappears after 1 hour, when it dies, or when you dismiss it as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action). The censer can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

When you take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to remove the stopper of this painted brass bottle, a cloud of thick smoke flows out of it. At the end of your turn, the smoke disappears with a flash of harmless fire, and an [Efreeti](srd-5.2/14/efreeti/efreeti) appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you.
The first time the bottle is opened, the DM rolls on the following table to determine what happens.

rows: The [efreeti](srd-5.2/14/efreeti/efreeti) attacks you. After fighting for 5 rounds, the efreeti disappears, and the bottle loses its magic.

The [efreeti](srd-5.2/14/efreeti/efreeti) understands your languages and obeys your commands for 1 hour, after which it returns to the bottle, and a new stopper contains it. The stopper can't be removed for 24 hours. The next two times the bottle is opened, the same effect occurs. If the bottle is opened a fourth time, the efreeti escapes and disappears, and the bottle loses its magic.

The [efreeti](srd-5.2/14/efreeti/efreeti) understands your languages and can cast *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* once for you. It disappears when it grants the wish or after 1 hour, and the bottle loses its magic.

content.text: This gem contains a mote of elemental energy. When you take a Utilize action to break the gem, an elemental is summoned (see the System Reference Document for its stat block), and the gem ceases to be magical. The elemental appears in an unoccupied space as close to the broken gem as possible, understands your languages, obeys your commands, and takes its turn immediately after you on your Initiative count. The elemental disappears after 1 hour, when it dies, or when you dismiss it as a Bonus Action.
The type of gem determines the elemental, as shown in the following table.

When you drink this potion, you are cured of all magical contagions. In addition, the following conditions end on you: [Blinded](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/blinded), [Deafened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/deafened), [Paralyzed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/paralyzed), and [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned).
The clear, red liquid has tiny bubbles of light in it.

You gain a +1 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) while you wear this armor. You are considered trained with this armor even if you lack training with Medium or Heavy armor.

content.text: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has no string. Each time you pull your arm back in a firing motion, a magical arrow made of golden energy appears nocked and ready to fire. An arrow produced by this weapon deals Force damage instead of Piercing damage on a hit, and it disappears after it hits or misses its target. Until it disappears, the arrow emits [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 20-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 20 feet.
This weapon has the following additional properties.

content.label: Arrow of Restraint
content.text: Whenever you use this weapon to make a ranged attack against a creature, you can try to restrain the target instead of dealing damage to it. If the arrow hits, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or have the [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) condition for 1 minute. As an action, a creature [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) by an arrow can make a DC 20 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check to try to break the restraint, ending the effect on itself on a successful check.

content.label: Arrow of Transport
content.text: As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can fire one energy arrow from this weapon at a target you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The target can be either a willing Medium or smaller creature or an object that isn't being worn or carried, provided the object is small enough to fit inside a 5-foot [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube). The arrow teleports the target to an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of you.

content.label: Energy Ladder
content.text: As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can loose a flurry of energy arrows from this weapon at a wall up to 60 feet away from yourself. The arrows become glowing rungs that stick out of the wall, forming a magical ladder up to 60 feet long on the wall. This ladder lasts for 1 minute before disappearing.

content.text: As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can open or close this bottle.

Opening the bottle causes thick smoke to billow out, forming a cloud that fills a 60-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) originating from the bottle. The area within the smoke is [Heavily Obscured](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/heavily-obscured).
Each minute the bottle remains open, the size of the [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) increases by 10 feet until it reaches its maximum size of 120 feet.

Closing the bottle causes the cloud to become fixed in place until it disperses after 10 minutes. A strong wind (such as that created by the *[Gust of Wind](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/gust-of-wind)* spell) disperses the cloud after 1 minute.

These crystal lenses fit over the eyes. They have 3 charges. While wearing them, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast *[Charm Person](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/charm-person)* (save DC 13). For 1 charge, you cast the level 1 version of the spell. You increase the spell's level by one for each additional charge you expend. The lenses regain all expended charges daily at dawn.

These crystal lenses fit over the eyes. While wearing them, your vision improves significantly out to a range of 1 foot, granting you [Darkvision](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkvision) within that range and [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Intelligence ([Investigation](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/investigation)) checks made to examine something within that range.

These crystal lenses fit over the eyes. While wearing them, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Wisdom ([Perception](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/perception)) checks that rely on sight. In conditions of clear visibility, you can make out details of even extremely distant creatures and objects as small as 2 feet across.

Each *Ring of Elemental Command* is linked to one of the four Elemental Planes. The DM chooses or randomly determines the linked plane. For example, a *Ring of Elemental Command (air)* is linked to the Elemental Plane of Air. Every *Ring of Elemental Command* has the following two properties:

items.label: Elemental Bane
items.text: While wearing the ring, you have Advantage on attack rolls against Elementals and they have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

items.label: Elemental Compulsion
items.text: While wearing the ring, you can take a Magic action to try to compel an Elemental you see within 60 feet of yourself. The Elemental makes a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the Elemental has the Charmed condition until the start your next turn, and you determine what it does with its move and action on its next turn.

content.label: Elemental Focus
content.text: While wearing the ring, you benefit from additional properties corresponding to the ring's linked Elemental Plane:

items.label: Air
items.text: You know Auran, you have Resistance to Lightning damage, and you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover.

items.label: Earth
items.text: You know Terran, and you have Resistance to Acid damage. Terrain composed of rubble, rocks, or dirt isn't Difficult Terrain for you. In addition, you can move through solid earth or rock as if those areas were Difficult Terrain without disturbing the matter through which you pass. If you end your turn in solid earth or rock, you are shunted out to the nearest unoccupied space you last occupied.

items.label: Fire
items.text: You know Ignan, and you have Immunity to Fire damage.

items.label: Water
items.text: You know Aquan, you gain a Swim Speed of 60 feet, and you can breathe underwater.

content.label: Spellcasting
content.text: The ring has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the ring, you can cast a spell from it. Choose the spell from the list of available spells based on the Elemental Plane the ring is linked to, as shown in the following table. The table indicates how many charges you must expend to cast the spell, which has a save DC of 18.

rows: *Chain Lightning* (3 charges), *Feather Fall* (0 charges), *Gust of Wind* (2 charges), *Wind Wall* (1 charge)
*Earthquake* (5 charges), *Stone Shape* (2 charges), *Stoneskin* (3 charges), *Wall of Stone* (3 charges)
*Burning Hands* (1 charge), *Fireball* (2 charges), *Fire Storm* (4 charges), *Wall of Fire* (3 charges)
*Create or Destroy Water* (1 charge), *Ice Storm* (2 charges), *Tsunami* (5 charges), *Wall of Ice* (3 charges), *Water Walk* (2 charges)

content.text: While touching this 5-pound stone to the ground, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to summon an [Earth Elemental](srd-5.2/14/earth-elemental/earth-elemental). The elemental appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 30 feet of yourself, obeys your commands, and takes its turn immediately after you on your [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) count. The elemental disappears after 1 hour, when it dies, or when you dismiss it as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action). The stone can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

A *Figurine of Wondrous Power* is a statuette small enough to fit in a pocket. If you take a Magic action to throw the figurine to a point on the ground within 60 feet of yourself, the figurine becomes a living creature specified in the figurine's description below. If the space where the creature would appear is occupied by other creatures or objects, or if there isn't enough space for the creature, the figurine doesn't become a creature.

The creature is Friendly to you and your allies. It understands your languages, obeys your commands, and takes its turn immediately after you on your Initiative count. If you issue no commands, the creature defends itself but takes no other actions.

The creature exists for a duration specific to each figurine. At the end of the duration, the creature reverts to its figurine form. It reverts to a figurine early if its creature form drops to 0 Hit Points or if you take a Magic action while touching the creature to make it revert to figurine form. When the creature becomes a figurine again, its property can't be used again until a certain amount of time has passed, as specified below.

content.label: Bronze Griffon (Rare)
content.text: This bronze statuette is of a griffon rampant. It can become a Griffon for up to 6 hours. Once it has been used, it can't be used again until 5 days have passed.

content.label: Ebony Fly (Rare)
content.text: This ebony statuette, carved in the likeness of a horsefly, can become a Giant Fly for up to 12 hours and can be ridden as a mount. Once it has been used, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed.

content.label: Golden Lions (Rare)
content.text: These gold statuettes of lions are always created in pairs. You can use one figurine or both simultaneously. Each can become a Lion for up to 1 hour. Once a lion has been used, it can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

content.label: Ivory Goats (Rare)
content.text: These ivory statuettes of goats are always created in sets of three. Each goat looks unique and functions differently from the others. Their properties are as follows:

items.label: Goat of Terror
items.text: This figurine can become a Giant Goat for up to 3 hours. The goat can't attack, but you can (harmlessly) remove its horns and use them as weapons. One horn becomes a +1 Lance, and the other becomes a +2 Longsword. Removing a horn requires a Magic action, and the weapons disappear and the horns return when the goat reverts to figurine form. While you ride the goat, any Hostile creature that starts its turn within a 30-foot Emanation originating from the goat must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute, until you are no longer riding the goat, or until the goat reverts to figurine form. The Frightened creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once it succeeds on the save, a creature is immune to this effect for the next 24 hours. Once the figurine has been used, it can't be used again until 15 days have passed.

items.label: Goat of Traveling
items.text: This figurine can become a Large goat with the same statistics as a Riding Horse. It has 24 charges, and each hour or portion thereof it spends in goat form costs 1 charge. While it has charges, you can use it as often as you wish. When it runs out of charges, it reverts to a figurine and can't be used again until 7 days have passed, when it regains all expended charges.

items.label: Goat of Travail
items.text: This figurine can become a Giant Goat for up to 3 hours. Once it has been used, it can't be used again until 30 days have passed.

content.label: Marble Elephant (Rare)
content.text: This marble statuette resembles a trumpeting elephant. It can become an Elephant for up to 24 hours. Once it has been used, it can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

content.label: Obsidian Steed (Very Rare)
content.text: This polished obsidian horse can become a Nightmare for up to 24 hours. The nightmare fights only to defend itself. Once it has been used, it can't be used again until 5 days have passed.

The figurine has a 10 percent chance each time you use it to ignore your orders, including a command to revert to figurine form. If you mount the nightmare while it is ignoring your orders, you and the nightmare are instantly transported to a random location on the plane of Hades, where the nightmare reverts to figurine form.

content.label: Onyx Dog (Rare)
content.text: This onyx statuette of a dog can become a Mastiff for up to 6 hours. The mastiff has an Intelligence of 8 and can speak Common. It also has Blindsight with a range of 60 feet. Once it has been used, it can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

content.label: Serpentine Owl (Rare)
content.text: This serpentine statuette of an owl can become a Giant Owl for up to 8 hours. The owl can communicate telepathically with you at any range if you and it are on the same plane of existence. Once it has been used, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed.

content.label: Silver Raven (Uncommon)
content.text: This silver statuette of a raven can become a Raven for up to 12 hours. Once it has been used, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed. While in raven form, the figurine grants you the ability to cast *Animal Messenger* on it.

While the weapon is ablaze, it deals an extra 2d6 Fire damage on a hit. The flames last until you take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to issue the command again or until you drop, stow, or sheathe the weapon.

This object appears as a wooden box that measures 12 inches long, 6 inches wide, and 6 inches deep. It weighs 4 pounds and floats. It can be opened to store items inside. This item also has three command words, each requiring a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to use:

items.label: First Command Word
items.text: The box unfolds into a Rowboat.

items.label: Second Command Word
items.text: The box unfolds into a Keelboat.

items.label: Third Command Word
items.text: The *Folding Boat* folds back into a box if no creatures are aboard. Any objects in the vessel that can't fit inside the box remain outside the box as it folds. Any objects in the vessel that can fit inside the box do so.

content.text: When the box becomes a vessel, its weight becomes that of a normal vessel its size, and anything that was stored in the box remains in the boat.

Statistics for the [Rowboat](srd-5.2/06/mounts-and-vehicles/large-vehicles/rowboat) and [Keelboat](srd-5.2/06/mounts-and-vehicles/large-vehicles/keelboat) appear in the System Reference Document. If either vessel is reduced to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points), the *Folding Boat* is destroyed.

When you hit with an attack roll using this magic weapon, the target takes an extra 1d6 Cold damage. In addition, while you hold the weapon, you have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to Fire damage.

In freezing temperatures, the weapon sheds [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 10-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 10 feet.
When you draw this weapon, you can extinguish all nonmagical flames within 30 feet of yourself. Once used, this property can't be used again for 1 hour.
