content.text: While wearing this belt, your Strength score changes to a score granted by the belt. The item has no effect on you if your Strength without the belt is equal to or greater than the belt's score.
The type of giant determines the score and the belt's rarity, as shown in the following table.

rows: *Belt of Giant Strength (frost)* or *Belt of Giant Strength (stone)*

content.text: Your Strength score is 19 while you wear these gauntlets. They have no effect on you if your Strength is 19 or higher without them.
This prism has 50 charges. While you are holding it, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action and use one of three command words to cause one of the following effects:

items.label: First Command Word
items.text: The gem sheds [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 30-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 30 feet. This effect doesn't expend a charge. It lasts until you take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to repeat the command word or until you use another function of the gem.

items.label: Second Command Word
items.text: You expend 1 charge and cause the gem to fire a brilliant beam of light at one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have the [Blinded](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/blinded) condition for 1 minute. The creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

items.label: Third Command Word
items.text: You expend 5 charges and cause the gem to flare with intense light in a 30-foot [Cone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cone). Each creature in the [Cone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cone) makes a saving throw as if struck by the beam created with the second command word.

content.text: When all of the gem's charges are expended, the gem becomes a nonmagical jewel worth 50 GP.

This gem has 3 charges. As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can expend 1 charge. For the next 10 minutes, you have [Truesight](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/truesight) out to 120 feet when you peer through the gem.
The gem regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When you hit a Giant with this weapon, the Giant takes an extra 2d6 damage of the weapon's type and must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or have the [Prone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/prone) condition.

While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class). You can also take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to cause the armor to assume the appearance of a normal set of clothing or some other kind of armor. You decide what it looks like—including color, style, and accessories—but the armor retains its normal bulk and weight. The illusory appearance lasts until you use this property again or doff the armor.

If you're hit by an attack roll made with a Ranged or Thrown weapon while wearing these gloves, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to reduce the damage by 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier if you have a free hand. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can catch the ammunition or weapon if it is small enough for you to hold in that hand.
While wearing these gloves, you have a Climb Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your Speed, and you gain a +5 bonus to Strength (Athletics) checks made to climb or swim.
These gloves are imperceptible while worn. While wearing them, you gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity ([Sleight of Hand](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/sleight-of-hand)) checks.

While wearing these dark lenses, you have [Darkvision](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkvision) out to 60 feet. If you already have [Darkvision](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkvision), wearing the goggles increases its range by 60 feet.

When you drink this potion, your Strength score changes for 1 hour. The type of giant determines the score (see the table below). The potion has no effect on you if your Strength is equal to or greater than that score.
This potion's transparent liquid has floating in it a sliver of light resembling a giant's fingernail.

rows: *Potion of Giant Strength (frost)* or *Potion of Giant Strength (stone)*

content.text: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The weapon has 5 charges. You can expend 1 charge and make a ranged attack with the weapon, hurling it as if it had [Thrown](srd-5.2/06/weapons/properties/thrown) with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.

If the attack hits, the weapon unleashes a thunderclap audible out to 300 feet. The target and every creature within 30 feet of it other than you must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or have the [Stunned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/stunned) condition until the end of your next turn. Immediately after hitting or missing, the weapon flies back to your hand. The weapon regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn.

content.label: Giant's Bane
content.text: While you are attuned to the weapon and wearing either a *[Belt of Giant Strength](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/belt-of-giant-strength)* or *[Gauntlets of Ogre Power](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/gauntlets-of-ogre-power)* to which you are also attuned, you gain the following benefits:

items.label: Giants' Bane
items.text: When you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this weapon against a Giant, the creature must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or die.

items.label: Might of Giants
items.text: The Strength score bestowed by your *[Belt of Giant Strength](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/belt-of-giant-strength)* or *[Gauntlets of Ogre Power](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/gauntlets-of-ogre-power)* increases by 4, to a maximum of 30.

content.text: While wearing this hat, you can cast the *[Disguise Self](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/disguise-self)* spell. The spell ends if the hat is removed.
This pointed hat has the following properties.

content.label: Spellcasting Focus
content.text: While holding the hat, you can use it as a [Spellcasting Focus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/spellcasting-focus) for your Wizard spells. Any spell you cast using the hat gains a special Somatic component: you must reach into the hat and "pull" the spell out of it.

content.label: Unknown Spell
content.text: While holding the hat, you can try to cast a level 1+ spell you don't know. The spell must be on the Wizard spell list, it must be of a level you can cast, and it can't have Material components costing more than 1,000 GP. Once you decide on the spell, you must expend a spell slot of the spell's level. Then, to determine whether you cast the spell, make an Intelligence ([Arcana](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/arcana)) check (DC 10 plus the spell's level). On a successful check, you cast the spell using its normal casting time, and you can't use this property again until you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest). On a failed check, you fail to cast the spell and a random effect occurs instead, determined by rolling on the following table.
Any spell you cast from the hat uses your spell save DC and spell attack bonus.

rows: You cast a random spell determined by rolling 1d10: on a **1**, *[Enlarge/Reduce](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/enlarge-reduce)* (enlarge effect); on a **2**, *[Enlarge/Reduce](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/enlarge-reduce)* (reduce effect); on a **3**, *[Faerie Fire](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/faerie-fire)*; on a **4**, *[Fireball](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/fireball)*; on a **5**, *[Gust of Wind](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/gust-of-wind)*; on a **6**, *[Invisibility](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/invisibility)* (cast on yourself); on a **7**, *[Lightning Bolt](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/lightning-bolt)*; on an **8**, *[Phantasmal Force](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/phantasmal-force)*; on a **9**, *[Polymorph](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/polymorph)*; on a **10**, *[Stinking Cloud](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/stinking-cloud)*.
You have the [Stunned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/stunned) condition until the end of your next turn, believing something awesome just happened.
A harmless swarm of butterflies fills a 10-foot [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube) within 30 feet of yourself. The swarm disperses after 1 minute.
You pull a nonmagical object out of the hat. Roll 1d4 to determine the object: on a **1**, a vial of Acid; on a **2**, a flask of Alchemist's Fire; on a **3**, a Crowbar; on a **4**, a lit Torch.
You suffer a bout of "magic sickness" and have the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition for 1 hour.
You have the [Petrified](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/petrified) condition until the end of your next turn.

You pull a nonmagical object out of the hat. Roll 1d4 to determine the object: on a **1**, a [Dagger](srd-5.2/06/weapons/dagger); on a **2**, a [Rope](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rope) with a [Grappling Hook](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/grappling-hook) tied to one end; on a **3**, a bag of [Caltrops](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/caltrops); on a **4**, a gem worth 50 GP.

A creature appears in an unoccupied space as close to you as possible. The creature isn't under your control and acts as it normally would, and it disappears after 1 hour or when it drops to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points). Roll 1d4 to determine the creature: on a **1**, a [Camel](srd-5.2/15/camel); on a **2**, a [Constrictor Snake](srd-5.2/15/constrictor-snake); on a **3**, an [Elephant](srd-5.2/15/elephant); on a **4**, a [Mule](srd-5.2/15/mule).
A [Hostile](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hostile) [Swarm of Bats](srd-5.2/15/swarm-of-bats) flies out of the hat, occupies your space, and attacks you.

A vertical, 10-foot-diameter, two-way portal to another plane of existence opens in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you and remains open until the end of your next turn. The DM determines where it leads.

You pull a magic item out of the hat. Roll 1d6 to determine the item's rarity: on a **1-3**, Common; on a **4-5**, Uncommon; on a **6**, Rare. The DM chooses the item, which disappears after 1 hour if it's not consumed or destroyed before then.

content.text: Your Intelligence score is 19 while you wear this headband. It has no effect on you if your Intelligence is 19 or higher without it.
This helm is set with 1d10 diamonds, 2d10 rubies, 3d10 fire opals, and 4d10 opals. Any gem pried from the helm crumbles to dust. When all the gems are removed or destroyed, the helm loses its magic.
You gain the following benefits while wearing the helm.

content.label: Diamond Light
content.text: As long as it has at least one diamond, the helm emits a 30-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation). When at least one Undead is within that area, the [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) is filled with [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light). Any Undead that starts its turn in that area takes 1d6 Radiant damage.

content.label: Fire Opal Flames
content.text: As long as the helm has at least one fire opal, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to cause one weapon you are holding to burst into flames. The flames emit [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 10-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 10 feet. The flames are harmless to you and the weapon. When you hit with an attack using the blazing weapon, the target takes an extra 1d6 Fire damage. The flames last until you take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to extinguish them or until you drop or stow the weapon.

content.label: Ruby Resistance
content.text: As long as the helm has at least one ruby, you have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to Fire damage.

content.label: Spells
content.text: You can cast one of the following spells (save DC 18), using one of the helm's gems of the specified type as a component: *[Daylight](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/daylight)* (opal), *[Fireball](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/fireball)* (fire opal), *[Prismatic Spray](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/prismatic-spray)* (diamond), or *[Wall of Fire](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wall-of-fire)* (ruby). The gem is destroyed when the spell is cast and disappears from the helm.

content.label: Taking Fire Damage
content.text: Roll 1d20 if you are wearing the helm and take Fire damage as a result of failing a saving throw against a spell. On a roll of 1, the helm emits beams of light from its remaining gems and is then destroyed. Each creature within a 60-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) originating from you must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or be struck by a beam, taking Radiant damage equal to the number of gems in the helm.
While wearing this helm, you can cast *[Comprehend Languages](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/comprehend-languages)* from it.

While wearing this helm, you have telepathy with a range of 30 feet, and you can cast *[Detect Thoughts](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/detect-thoughts)* or *[Suggestion](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/suggestion)* (save DC 13) from the helm. Once either spell is cast from the helm, that spell can't be cast from it again until the next dawn.
This helm has 3 charges. While wearing it, you can expend 1 charge to cast *[Teleport](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/teleport)* from it. The helm regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

This backpack has a central pouch and two side pouches, each of which is an extradimensional space. Each side pouch can hold up to 200 pounds of material, not exceeding a volume of 25 cubic feet. The central pouch can hold up to 500 pounds of material, not exceeding a volume of 64 cubic feet. The haversack always weighs 5 pounds, regardless of its contents.

Retrieving an item from the haversack requires a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action or a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) (your choice). When you reach into the haversack for a specific item, the item is always magically on top.

If any of its pouches is overloaded, pierced, or torn, the haversack ruptures and is destroyed. If the haversack is destroyed, its contents are lost forever, although an Artifact always turns up again somewhere. If the haversack is turned inside out, its contents spill forth unharmed, and the haversack must be put right before it can be used again.
Each pouch of the haversack holds enough air for 10 minutes of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.

Placing the haversack inside an extradimensional space created by a *[Bag of Holding](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/bag-of-holding)*, *[Portable Hole](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/portable-hole)*, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind [Total Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover) is sucked through it and deposited in a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a Fiend or an Undead with it, that creature takes an extra 2d10 Radiant damage.

While you hold the drawn weapon, it creates a 10-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) originating from you. You and all creatures [Friendly](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/friendly) to you in the [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. If you have 17 or more levels in the Paladin class, the size of the [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) increases to 30 feet.

data.subtitle: Weapon (Any Simple or Martial), Legendary (Requires Attunement by a Paladin)

content.text: You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to blow the horn, which emits a thunderous blast in a 30-foot [Cone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cone) that is audible out to 600 feet. Each creature in the [Cone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cone) makes a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d8 Thunder damage and has the [Deafened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/deafened) condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only. Glass or crystal objects in the [Cone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cone) that aren't being worn or carried take 10d8 Thunder damage.
Each use of the horn's magic has a 20 percent chance of causing the horn to explode. The explosion deals 10d6 Force damage to the user and destroys the horn.

You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to blow this horn. In response, warrior spirits from the plane of Ysgard appear in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of you. Each spirit uses the [Berserker](srd-5.2/14/berserkers/berserker) stat block and returns to Ysgard after 1 hour or when it drops to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points). The spirits look like living, breathing warriors, and they have [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to the [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) and [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) conditions. Once you use the horn, it can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

Four types of *Horn of Valhalla* are known to exist, each made of a different metal. The horn's type determines how many spirits it summons, as well as the requirement for its use. The DM chooses the horn's type or determines it randomly by rolling on the following table. If you blow the horn without meeting its requirement, the summoned spirits attack you.
If you meet the requirement, they are [Friendly](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/friendly) to you and your allies and follow your commands.

data.subtitle: Wondrous Item, Rare (Silver or Brass), Very Rare (Bronze), or Legendary (Iron)

content.text: These horseshoes come in a set of four. As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can touch one of the horseshoes to the hoof of a horse or similar creature, whereupon the horseshoe affixes itself to the hoof. Removing a horseshoe also takes a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action.

While all four shoes are affixed to the hooves of a horse or similar creature, they allow the creature to move normally while floating 4 inches above a surface. This effect means the creature can cross or stand above nonsolid or unstable surfaces, such as water or lava. The creature leaves no tracks and ignores [Difficult Terrain](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/difficult-terrain). In addition, the creature can travel for up to 12 hours a day without gaining [Exhaustion](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/exhaustion) levels from extended travel.

These horseshoes come in a set of four. As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can touch one of the horseshoes to the hoof of a horse or similar creature, whereupon the horseshoe affixes itself to the hoof. Removing a horseshoe also takes a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action.
While all four horseshoes are attached to the same creature, its [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) is increased by 30 feet.

This iron rod has a button on one end. You can take a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to press the button, which causes the rod to become magically fixed in place. Until you or another creature takes a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to push the button again, the rod doesn't move, even if it defies gravity. The rod can hold up to 8,000 pounds of weight. More weight causes the rod to deactivate and fall. A creature can take a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to make a DC 30 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check, moving the fixed rod up to 10 feet on a successful check.
Roughly marble sized, Ioun Stones are named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of Ioun Stones exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you take a Magic action to toss an *Ioun Stone* into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of 1d3 feet, conferring its benefit to you while doing so. You can have up to three Ioun Stones orbiting your head at the same time.

Each *Ioun Stone* orbiting your head is considered to be an object you are wearing. The orbiting stone avoids contact with other creatures and objects, adjusting its orbit to avoid collisions and thwarting all attempts by other creatures to attack or snatch it.

As a Utilize action, you can seize and stow any number of Ioun Stones orbiting your head. If your Attunement to an *Ioun Stone* ends while it's orbiting your head, the stone falls as though you had dropped it.
The type of stone determines its rarity and effects.

content.label: Absorption (Very Rare)
content.text: While this pale lavender ellipsoid orbits your head, you can take a Reaction to cancel a spell of level 4 or lower cast by a creature you can see. A canceled spell has no effect, and any resources used to cast it are wasted. Once the stone has canceled 20 levels of spells, it burns out, turns dull gray, and loses its magic.

content.label: Agility (Very Rare)
content.text: Your Dexterity increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, while this deep-red sphere orbits your head.

content.label: Awareness (Rare)
content.text: While this dark-blue rhomboid orbits your head, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks.

content.label: Fortitude (Very Rare)
content.text: Your Constitution increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, while this pink rhomboid orbits your head.

content.label: Greater Absorption (Legendary)
content.text: While this marbled lavender and green ellipsoid orbits your head, you can take a Reaction to cancel a spell of level 8 or lower cast by a creature you can see. A canceled spell has no effect, and any resources used to cast it are wasted. Once the stone has canceled 20 levels of spells, it burns out, turns dull gray, and loses its magic.

content.label: Insight (Very Rare)
content.text: Your Wisdom increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, while this incandescent blue sphere orbits your head.

content.label: Intellect (Very Rare)
content.text: Your Intelligence increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, while this marbled scarlet and blue sphere orbits your head.

content.label: Leadership (Very Rare)
content.text: Your Charisma increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, while this marbled pink and green sphere orbits your head.

content.label: Mastery (Legendary)
content.text: Your Proficiency Bonus increases by 1 while this pale green prism orbits your head.

content.label: Protection (Rare)
content.text: You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while this dusty-rose prism orbits your head.

content.label: Regeneration (Legendary)
content.text: You regain 15 Hit Points at the end of each hour this pearly white spindle orbits your head if you have at least 1 Hit Point.

content.label: Reserve (Rare)
content.text: This vibrant purple prism stores spells cast into it, holding them until you use them. The stone can store up to 4 levels of spells at a time. When found, it contains 1d4 levels of stored spells chosen by the DM.

Any creature can cast a spell of level 1 through 4 into the stone by touching it as the spell is cast. The spell has no effect, other than to be stored in the stone. If the stone can't hold the spell, the spell is expended without effect. The level of the slot used to cast the spell determines how much space it uses.

While this stone orbits your head, you can cast any spell stored in it. The spell uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell. The spell cast from the stone is no longer stored in it, freeing up space.

content.label: Strength (Very Rare)
content.text: Your Strength increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, while this pale blue rhomboid orbits your head.

content.label: Sustenance (Rare)
content.text: You don't need to eat or drink while this clear spindle orbits your head.

This rusty iron sphere measures 3 inches in diameter and weighs 1 pound. You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to throw the sphere at a Huge or smaller creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. As the sphere moves through the air, it opens into a tangle of metal bands.

Make a ranged attack roll with an attack bonus equal to your Dexterity modifier plus your [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency). On a hit, the target has the [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) condition until you take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to issue a command that releases it. Doing so or missing with the attack causes the bands to contract and become a sphere once more.

A creature that can touch the bands, including the one [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained), can take an action to make a DC 20 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check to break the iron bands. On a successful check, the item is destroyed, and the [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) creature is freed. On a failed check, any further attempts made by that creature automatically fail until 24 hours have elapsed.
Once the bands are used, they can't be used again until the next dawn.

While holding this brass-stoppered iron flask, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to target a creature that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. If the flask is empty and the target is native to a plane of existence other than the one you're on, the target must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or be trapped in the flask. If the target has been trapped by the flask before, it has [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on the save. Once trapped, a creature remains in the flask until released. The flask can hold only one creature at a time. A creature trapped in the flask doesn't age and doesn't need to breathe, eat, or drink.

You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to remove the flask's stopper and release the creature in the flask. The creature then obeys your commands for 1 hour, understanding those commands even if it doesn't know the language in which the commands are given. If you issue no commands or give the creature a command that is likely to result in its death or imprisonment, it defends itself but otherwise takes no actions. At the end of the duration, the creature acts in accordance with its normal disposition and alignment.

An *[Identify](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/identify)* spell reveals if the flask contains a creature, but the only way to determine the type of creature is to open the flask. A newly discovered *Iron Flask* might already contain a creature chosen by the DM or determined randomly by rolling on the following table (see the System Reference Document for the creature's stat block).
Each time you make an attack roll with this magic weapon and hit, you can have it deal Lightning damage instead of Piercing damage.

content.label: Lightning Bolt
content.text: When you throw this weapon at a target no farther than 120 feet from you, you can forgo making a ranged attack roll and instead turn the weapon into a bolt of lightning. This bolt forms a 5-foot-wide [Line](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/line) between you and the target. The target and each other creature in the [Line](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/line) (excluding you) makes a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d6 Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Immediately after dealing this damage, the weapon reappears in your hand. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

While lit, this hooded lantern burns for 6 hours on 1 pint of oil, shedding [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 30-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 30 feet. [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) creatures and objects are visible as long as they are in the lantern's [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light). You can take a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action to lower the hood, reducing the lantern's light to [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) in a 5-foot radius.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While the weapon is on your person, you also gain a +1 bonus to saving throws.

content.label: Luck
content.text: If the weapon is on your person, you can call on its luck (no action required) to reroll one failed [D20 Test](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/d20-test) if you don't have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition. You must use the second roll. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

content.label: Wish
content.text: The weapon has 1d3 charges. While holding it, you can expend 1 charge and cast *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* from it. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn. The weapon loses this property if it has no charges.

content.text: When you hit a Fiend or an Undead with this magic weapon, that creature takes an extra 2d6 Radiant damage. If the target has 25 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) or fewer after taking this damage, it must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be destroyed. On a successful save, the creature has the [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) condition until the end of your next turn.

content.label: Light
content.text: While you hold this weapon, it sheds [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 20-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 20 feet.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The bonus increases to +3 when you use the weapon to attack a Construct.

When you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this weapon, the target takes an extra 7 Bludgeoning damage, or 14 Bludgeoning damage if it's a Construct. If a Construct has 25 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) or fewer after taking this damage, it is destroyed.

This magic weapon has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the weapon, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action and expend 1 charge to release a wave of terror from it. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) condition for 1 minute. While [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) in this way, a creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't make [Opportunity Attacks](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/opportunity-attacks). For its action, it can use only the [Dash](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dash) action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If it has nowhere it can move, the creature can take the [Dodge](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dodge) action. At the end of each of its turns, a creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws against spells while you wear this cloak.

This book contains health and diet tips, and its words are charged with magic. If you spend 48 hours over a period of 6 days or fewer studying the book's contents and practicing its guidelines, your Constitution increases by 2, to a maximum of 30. The manual then loses its magic, but regains it in a century.

This book describes fitness exercises, and its words are charged with magic. If you spend 48 hours over a period of 6 days or fewer studying the book's contents and practicing its guidelines, your Strength increases by 2, to a maximum of 30. The manual then loses its magic, but regains it in a century.

This tome contains information and incantations necessary to make a particular type of golem. The DM chooses the type or determines it randomly by rolling on the accompanying table. To decipher and use the manual, you must be a spellcaster with at least two level 5 spell slots. A creature that can't use a *Manual of Golems* and attempts to read it takes 6d6 Psychic damage.

To create a golem, you must spend the time shown on the table, working without interruption with the manual at hand and resting no more than 8 hours per day. You must also pay the specified cost to purchase supplies.

Once you finish creating the golem, the book is consumed in eldritch flames. The golem becomes animate when the ashes of the manual are sprinkled on it. See the System Reference Document for the golem's stat block. The golem is under your control, and it understands and obeys your commands.

This book contains coordination and balance exercises, and its words are charged with magic. If you spend 48 hours over a period of 6 days or fewer studying the book's contents and practicing its guidelines, your Dexterity increases by 2, to a maximum of 30. The manual then loses its magic, but regains it in a century.

The medallion has 5 charges. While wearing it, you can expend 1 charge to cast *[Detect Thoughts](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/detect-thoughts)* (save DC 13) from it. The medallion regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn.

When this 4-foot-tall, 2-foot-wide mirror is viewed indirectly, its surface shows faint images of creatures. The mirror weighs 50 pounds, and it has AC 11, HP 10, [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to Poison and Psychic damage, and [Vulnerability](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/vulnerability) to Bludgeoning damage. It shatters and is destroyed when reduced to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points).

If the mirror is hanging on a vertical surface and you are within 5 feet of it, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action and use a command word to activate it. It remains activated until you take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action and repeat the command word to deactivate it.

Any creature other than you that sees its reflection in the activated mirror while within 30 feet of the mirror must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be trapped, along with anything it is wearing or carrying, in one of the mirror's twelve extradimensional cells. A creature that knows the mirror's nature makes the save with [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage), and Constructs succeed on the save automatically.

An extradimensional cell is an infinite expanse filled with thick fog that reduces visibility to 10 feet. Creatures trapped in the mirror's cells don't age, and they don't need to eat, drink, or sleep. A creature trapped within a cell can escape using magic that permits planar travel. Otherwise, the creature is confined to the cell until freed.

If the mirror traps a creature but its twelve extradimensional cells are already occupied, the mirror frees one trapped creature at random to accommodate the new prisoner. A freed creature appears in an unoccupied space within sight of the mirror but facing away from it. If the mirror is shattered, all creatures it contains are freed and appear in unoccupied spaces near it.

While within 5 feet of the mirror, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to name one creature trapped in it or call out a particular cell by number. The creature named or contained in the named cell appears as an image on the mirror's surface. You and the creature can then communicate.

In a similar way, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action and use a second command word to free one creature trapped in the mirror. The freed creature appears, along with its possessions, in the unoccupied space nearest to the mirror and facing away from it.

Placing the mirror inside an extradimensional space created by a *[Bag of Holding](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/bag-of-holding)*, *[Portable Hole](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/portable-hole)*, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind [Total Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover) is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.
Mithral is a light, flexible metal. Armor made of this substance can be worn under normal clothes.
If the armor normally imposes Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks or has a Strength requirement, the mithral version of the armor doesn't.

content.text: While wearing this necklace, you can breathe normally in any environment, and you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws made to avoid or end the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition.

This necklace has 1d6 + 3 beads hanging from it. You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to detach a bead and throw it up to 60 feet away. When it reaches the end of its trajectory, the bead detonates as a level 3 *[Fireball](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/fireball)* (save DC 15).
You can hurl multiple beads, or even the whole necklace, at one time. When you do so, increase the damage of the Fireball by 1d6 for each bead after the first (maximum 12d6).

This necklace has 1d4 + 2 magic beads made from aquamarine, black pearl, or topaz. It also has many nonmagical beads made from stones such as amber, bloodstone, citrine, coral, jade, pearl, or quartz. If a magic bead is removed from the necklace, that bead loses its magic.

Six types of magic beads exist. The DM decides the type of each bead on the necklace or determines it randomly by rolling on the table below. A necklace can have more than one bead of the same type. To use one, you must be wearing the necklace. Each bead contains a spell that you can cast from it as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) (using your spell save DC if a save is necessary). Once a magic bead's spell is cast, that bead can't be used again until the next dawn.

content.text: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

content.label: Life Stealing
content.text: The weapon has 1d8 + 1 charges. When you attack a creature that has fewer than 100 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) with this weapon and roll a 20 on the d20 for the attack roll, the creature must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be slain instantly as the sword tears its life force from its body. Constructs and Undead succeed on the save automatically. The weapon loses 1 charge if the creature is slain. When the weapon has no charges remaining, it loses this property.

content.text: This fine wooden box contains 1d4 pots of pigment and a brush (weighing 1 pound in total). Using the brush and expending 1 pot of pigment, you can paint any number of three-dimensional objects and terrain features (such as walls, doors, trees, flowers, weapons, webs, and pits), provided these elements are all confined to a 20-foot [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube). The effort takes 10 minutes (regardless of the number of elements you create), during which time you must remain in the [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube), and requires [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration). If your [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) is broken or you leave the [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube) before the work is done, all the painted elements vanish, and the pot of pigment is wasted.

When the work is done, all the painted objects and terrain features become real. Thus, painting a door on a wall creates an actual door, which can be opened to whatever is beyond. Painting a pit creates a real pit, the entire depth of which must lie within the 20-foot [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube).

No object created by a pot of pigment can have a value greater than 25 GP, and the total value of all objects created by a pot of pigment can't exceed 500 GP. If you paint objects of greater value (such as a large pile of gold), they look authentic, but close inspection reveals they're made from paste, cookies, or some other worthless material.
If you paint a form of energy such as fire or lightning, the energy dissipates as soon as you complete the painting, doing no harm.

When you nock an arrow on this bow, it whispers in Elvish, "Swift defeat to my enemies." When you use this weapon to make a ranged attack, you can utter or sign the following command words: "Swift death to you who have wronged me." The target of your attack becomes your sworn enemy until it dies or until dawn 7 days later. You can have only one such sworn enemy at a time. When your sworn enemy dies, you can choose a new one after the next dawn.

When you make a ranged attack roll with this weapon against your sworn enemy, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on the roll. In addition, your target gains no benefit from [Half Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover) or [Three-Quarters Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover), and you suffer no [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) due to long range. If the attack hits, your sworn enemy takes an extra 3d6 Piercing damage.
While your sworn enemy lives, you have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on attack rolls with all other weapons.

content.text: One vial of this oil can cover one Medium or smaller creature, along with the equipment it's wearing and carrying (one additional vial is required for each size category above Medium). Applying the oil takes 10 minutes. The affected creature then gains the effect of the *[Etherealness](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/etherealness)* spell for 1 hour.
Beads of this cloudy, gray oil form on the outside of its container and quickly evaporate.

One vial of this oil can coat one Melee weapon or twenty pieces of ammunition, but only ammunition and Melee weapons that are nonmagical and deal Slashing or Piercing damage are affected. Applying the oil takes 1 minute, after which the oil magically seeps into whatever it coats, turning the coated weapon into a +3 Weapon or the coated ammunition into +3 Ammunition.
This clear, gelatinous oil sparkles with tiny, ultrathin silver shards.

One vial of this oil can cover one Medium or smaller creature, along with the equipment it's wearing and carrying (one additional vial is required for each size category above Medium). Applying the oil takes 10 minutes. The affected creature then gains the effect of the *[Freedom of Movement](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/freedom-of-movement)* spell for 8 hours.

Alternatively, the oil can be poured on the ground as a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, where it covers a 10-foot square, duplicating the effect of the *[Grease](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/grease)* spell in that area for 8 hours.
This sticky, black unguent is thick and heavy, but it flows quickly when poured.

While this pearl is on your person, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to regain one expended spell slot of level 3 or lower. Once you use the pearl, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

content.text: While wearing this pendant, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to regain 2d4 + 2 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points). Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.
In addition, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws to avoid or end the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition while you wear this pendant.

This delicate silver chain has a brilliant-cut black gem pendant. While you wear it, you have [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition and Poison damage.
While wearing this pendant, you gain the following benefits.

content.label: Life Preservation
content.text: Whenever you make a [Death Saving Throw](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/death-saving-throw), you can change a roll of 9 or lower to a 10, turning a failed save into a successful one.

content.label: Natural Healing Boost
content.text: Whenever you roll a [Hit Point Die](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-point-dice) to regain [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points), double the number of [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) it restores.

The next time you see a creature within 10 minutes after drinking this philter, you are [charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) by that creature and have the [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) condition for 1 hour.
This rose-hued, effervescent liquid contains one easy-to-miss bubble shaped like a heart.

These pipes have 3 charges and regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to play them and expend 1 charge to create an eerie, spellbinding tune. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) condition for 1 minute. A creature that fails the save repeats it at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on its save is immune to the effect of these pipes for 24 hours.

While these pipes are on your person, ordinary [rats](srd-5.2/15/rat) and [giant rats](srd-5.2/15/giant-rat) are [Indifferent](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/indifferent) toward you and won't attack you unless you threaten or harm them.

The pipes have 3 charges and regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. If you play the pipes as a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to expend 1 to 3 charges, calling forth one [Swarm of Rats](srd-5.2/15/swarm-of-rats) with each expended charge if enough rats are within half a mile of you to be called in this fashion (as determined by the DM). If there aren't enough rats to form a swarm, the charge is wasted. Called swarms move toward the music by the shortest available route but aren't under your control otherwise.

Whenever a Swarm of Rats that isn't under another creature's control comes within 30 feet of you while you are playing the pipes, the swarm makes a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, the swarm behaves as it normally would and can't be swayed by the pipes' music for the next 24 hours. On a failed save, the swarm is swayed by the pipes' music and becomes [Friendly](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/friendly) to you and your allies for as long as you continue to play the pipes each round as a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action. A [Friendly](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/friendly) swarm obeys your commands. If you issue no commands to a [Friendly](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/friendly) swarm, it defends itself but otherwise takes no actions. If a [Friendly](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/friendly) swarm starts its turn more than 30 feet away from you, your control over that swarm ends, and the swarm behaves as it normally would and can't be swayed by the pipes' music for the next 24 hours.

While you're wearing this armor, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action and use a command word to gain the effect of the *[Etherealness](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/etherealness)* spell. The spell ends immediately if you remove the armor or take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to repeat the command word. This property of the armor can't be used again until the next dawn.
