content.text: This fine black cloth, soft as silk, is folded up to the dimensions of a handkerchief. It unfolds into a circular sheet 6 feet in diameter.

You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to unfold a *Portable Hole* and place it on or against a solid surface, whereupon the *Portable Hole* creates an extradimensional hole 10 feet deep. The cylindrical space within the hole exists on a different plane of existence, so it can't be used to create open passages. Any creature inside an open *Portable Hole* can exit the hole by climbing out of it.

You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to close a *Portable Hole* by taking hold of the edges of the cloth and folding it up. Folding the cloth closes the hole, and any creatures or objects within remain in the extradimensional space. No matter what's in it, the hole weighs next to nothing.

If the hole is folded up, a creature within the hole's extradimensional space can take an action to make a DC 10 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) check. On a successful check, the creature forces its way out and appears within 5 feet of the *Portable Hole*. A closed *Portable Hole* holds enough air for 1 hour of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.

Placing a *Portable Hole* inside an extradimensional space created by a *[Bag of Holding](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/bag-of-holding)*, *[Handy Haversack](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/handy-haversack)*, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind [Total Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover) is sucked through it and deposited in a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.
When you drink this potion, you can cast the level 3 version of the *[Animal Friendship](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/animal-friendship)* spell (save DC 13).
Agitating this potion's muddy liquid brings little bits into view: a fish scale, a hummingbird feather, a cat claw, or a squirrel hair.
When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of the *[Clairvoyance](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/clairvoyance)* spell (no [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) required).
An eyeball bobs in this potion's yellowish liquid but vanishes when the potion is opened.

When you drink this potion, you gain a [Climb Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/climb-speed) equal to your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) for 1 hour. During this time, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) checks to climb.
This potion is separated into brown, silver, and gray layers resembling bands of stone. Shaking the bottle fails to mix the colors.

When you drink this potion, you gain the "reduce" effect of the *[Enlarge/Reduce](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/enlarge-reduce)* spell for 1d4 hours (no [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) required).
The red in the potion's liquid continuously contracts to a tiny bead and then expands to color the clear liquid around it. Shaking the bottle fails to interrupt this process.

When you drink this potion, you gain a [Fly Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/fly-speed) equal to your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed) for 1 hour and can hover. If you're in the air when the potion wears off, you fall unless you have some other means of staying aloft.
This potion's clear liquid floats at the top of its container and has cloudy white impurities drifting in it.

When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of the *[Gaseous Form](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/gaseous-form)* spell for 1 hour (no [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) required) or until you end the effect as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action).
This potion's container seems to hold fog that moves and pours like water.

When you drink this potion, you gain the "enlarge" effect of the *[Enlarge/Reduce](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/enlarge-reduce)* spell for 10 minutes (no [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) required).
The red in the potion's liquid continuously expands from a tiny bead to color the clear liquid around it and then contracts. Shaking the bottle fails to interrupt this process.

You regain Hit Points when you drink this potion. The number of Hit Points depends on the potion's rarity, as shown in the table below. Whatever its potency, the potion's red liquid glimmers when agitated.

When you drink this potion, you gain 10 [Temporary Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/temporary-hit-points) that last for 1 hour. For the same duration, you are under the effect of the *[Bless](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/bless)* spell (no [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) required).
This potion's blue liquid bubbles and steams as if boiling.

This potion's container looks empty but feels as though it holds liquid. When you drink the potion, you have the [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) condition for 1 hour. The effect ends early if you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell.
For 1 minute after you drink this potion, you have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to all damage.
This potion's syrupy liquid looks like liquefied iron.

When you drink this potion, your physical age is reduced by 1d6 + 6 years, to a minimum of 13 years. Each time you subsequently drink a *Potion of Longevity*, there is 10 percent cumulative chance that you instead age by 1d6 + 6 years.
Suspended in this amber liquid is a tiny heart that, against all reason, is still beating. These ingredients vanish when the potion is opened.

When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of the *[Detect Thoughts](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/detect-thoughts)* spell (save DC 13) for 10 minutes (no [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) required).
This potion's dense, purple liquid has an ovoid cloud of pink floating in it.

This concoction looks, smells, and tastes like a *[Potion of Healing](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/potion-of-healing)* or another beneficial potion. However, it is actually poison masked by illusion magic. *[Identify](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/identify)* reveals its true nature.
If you drink this potion, you take 4d6 Poison damage and must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition for 1 hour.

When you drink this potion, you have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to one type of damage for 1 hour. The DM chooses the type or determines it randomly by rolling on the following table.

When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of the *[Haste](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/haste)* spell for 1 minute (no [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration) required) without suffering the wave of lethargy that typically occurs when the effect ends.
This potion's yellow fluid is streaked with black and swirls on its own.

When you drink this potion, it removes any [Exhaustion](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/exhaustion) levels you have and ends the [Poisoned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/poisoned) condition on you. For the next 24 hours, you regain the maximum number of [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) for any [Hit Point Die](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-point-dice) you spend.
This potion's crimson liquid regularly pulses with dull light, calling to mind a heartbeat.
You can breathe underwater for 24 hours after drinking this potion.
This potion's cloudy green fluid smells of the sea and has a jellyfish-like bubble floating in it.

This object looks like a feather. Different types of feather tokens exist, each with a different single-use effect. The DM chooses the kind of token or determines it randomly by rolling on the Feather Tokens table. The type of token determines its rarity.

content.label: Anchor
content.text: You can take a Magic action to touch the token to a boat or ship. For the next 24 hours, the vessel can't be moved by any means. Touching the token to the vessel again ends the effect. When the effect ends, the token disappears.

content.label: Bird
content.text: You can take a Magic action to toss the token 5 feet into the air. The token disappears and an enormous, multicolored bird takes its place. The bird has the statistics of a Roc, but it can't attack. It obeys your simple commands and can carry up to 500 pounds while flying at its maximum speed (16 miles per hour for a maximum of 144 miles per day, with a 1-hour rest for every 3 hours of flying) or 1,000 pounds at half that speed. The bird disappears after flying its maximum distance for a day or if it drops to 0 Hit Points. You can dismiss the bird as a Magic action.

content.label: Fan
content.text: If you are on a boat or ship, you can take a Magic action to toss the token up to 10 feet in the air. The token disappears, and a giant flapping fan takes its place. The fan floats and creates a strong wind. This wind can fill the sails of one ship, increasing its speed by 5 miles per hour for 8 hours. You can dismiss the fan as a Magic action.

content.label: Swan Boat
content.text: You can take a Magic action to touch the token to a body of water at least 60 feet in diameter. The token disappears, and a 50-foot-long, 20-foot-wide boat shaped like a swan takes its place. The boat is self-propelled and moves across water at a speed of 6 miles per hour. You can take a Magic action while on the boat to command it to move or to turn up to 90 degrees. The boat remains for 24 hours and then disappears. You can dismiss the boat as a Magic action.

content.label: Tree
content.text: You must be outdoors to use this token. You can take a Magic action to touch it to an unoccupied space on the ground. The token disappears, and in its place a nonmagical oak tree springs into existence. The tree is 60 feet tall and has a 5-foot-diameter trunk, and its branches at the top spread out in a 20-foot radius.

content.label: Whip
content.text: You can take a Magic action to throw the token to a point within 10 feet of yourself. The token disappears, and a floating whip takes its place. You can then take a Bonus Action to make a melee spell attack against a creature within 10 feet of the whip, with an attack bonus of +9. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 + 5 Force damage.

As a Bonus Action, you can direct the whip to fly up to 20 feet and repeat the attack against a creature within 10 feet of the whip. The whip disappears after 1 hour, when you take a Magic action to dismiss it, or when you die or have the Incapacitated condition.
You have a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While holding this weapon, you can cause it to emit green [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) out to 10 feet, either as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) or after you roll [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative), or you can extinguish the light as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action).

While holding this weapon, you can take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to alter its form, turning it into a 6-inch rod (for ease of storage) or a 10-foot pole, or reverting it a Quarterstaff; the weapon will elongate only as far as the surrounding space allows.
In certain forms, the weapon has the following additional properties.

content.label: Acrobatic Assist (Quarterstaff and 10-Foot Pole Forms Only)
content.text: While holding this weapon, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Dexterity ([Acrobatics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/acrobatics)) checks.

content.label: Attack Deflection (Quarterstaff Form Only)
content.text: When you are hit by an attack while holding the weapon, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to twirl the weapon around you, gaining a +5 bonus to your [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) against the triggering attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you. You can't use this property again until you finish a [Short](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/short-rest) or [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest).

content.label: Ranged Weapon (Quarterstaff Form Only)
content.text: This weapon has [Thrown](srd-5.2/06/weapons/properties/thrown) with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 120 feet. Immediately after you make a ranged attack with the weapon, it flies back to your hand.

Each of the quiver's three compartments connects to an extradimensional space that allows the quiver to hold numerous items while never weighing more than 2 pounds. The shortest compartment can hold up to 60 [Arrows](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ammunition), [Bolts](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/ammunition), or similar objects. The midsize compartment holds up to 18 [Javelins](srd-5.2/06/weapons/javelin) or similar objects. The longest compartment holds up to 6 long objects, such as bows, [Quarterstaffs](srd-5.2/06/weapons/quarterstaff), or [Spears](srd-5.2/06/weapons/spear).
You can draw any item the quiver contains as if doing so from a regular quiver or scabbard.
This ring has 3 charges, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the ring, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells (save DC 13) from it:

items.text: *[Animal Friendship](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/animal-friendship)*
*[Fear](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/fear)* (affects Beasts only)
*[Speak with Animals](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/speak-with-animals)*

content.text: While wearing this ring, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to summon a particular [Djinni](srd-5.2/14/djinni/djinni) from the Elemental Plane of Air. The djinni appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 120 feet of yourself. It remains as long as you maintain [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration), to a maximum of 1 hour, or until it drops to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points).

While summoned, the djinni is [Friendly](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/friendly) to you and your allies, and it obeys your commands. If you fail to command it, the djinni defends itself against attackers but takes no other actions.
After the djinni departs, it can't be summoned again for 24 hours, and the ring becomes nonmagical if the djinni dies.
Rings of Djinni Summoning are often created by the djinn they summon and given to mortals as gifts of friendship or tokens of esteem.

This ring has 3 charges, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. When you fail a Dexterity saving throw while wearing the ring, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to expend 1 charge to succeed on that save instead.
When you fall while wearing this ring, you descend 60 feet per round and take no damage from falling.

While you wear this ring, [Difficult Terrain](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/difficult-terrain) doesn't cost you extra movement. In addition, magic can neither reduce any of your Speeds nor cause you to have the [Paralyzed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/paralyzed) or [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) condition.

While wearing this ring, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to give yourself the [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) condition. You remain [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) until the ring is removed or until you take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to become visible again.
While wearing this ring, you can cast *[Jump](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/jump)* from it, but can target only yourself when you do so.

While wearing this ring, you are immune to magic that allows other creatures to read your thoughts, determine whether you are lying, know your alignment, or know your creature type. Creatures can telepathically communicate with you only if you allow it.

You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to cause the ring to become imperceptible until you take another [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to make it perceptible, until you remove the ring, or until you die.

If you die while wearing the ring, your soul enters it, unless it already houses a soul. You can remain in the ring or depart for the afterlife. As long as your soul is in the ring, you can telepathically communicate with any creature wearing it. A wearer can't prevent this telepathic communication.
You gain a +1 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) and saving throws while wearing this ring.

While wearing this ring, you regain 1d6 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) every 10 minutes if you have at least 1 [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points). If you lose a body part, the ring causes the missing part to regrow and return to full functionality after 1d6 + 1 days if you have at least 1 [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) the whole time.

You have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to one damage type while wearing this ring. The gemstone in the ring indicates the type, which the DM chooses or determines randomly by rolling on the following table.
You can cast *[Dancing Lights](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/dancing-lights)* or *[Light](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/light)* from the ring.
The ring has 6 charges and regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend its charges to use the properties below.

content.label: Faerie Fire
content.text: You can expend 1 charge to cast *[Faerie Fire](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/faerie-fire)* from the ring.

content.label: Lightning Spheres
content.text: You can expend 2 charges as a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to create up to four 3-foot-diameter spheres of lightning.

Each sphere appears in an unoccupied space you can see within 120 feet of yourself. The spheres last as long as you maintain [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration), up to 1 minute. Each sphere sheds [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) in a 30-foot radius.

As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can move each sphere up to 30 feet, but no farther than 120 feet away from yourself. The first time the sphere comes within 5 feet of a creature other than you that isn't behind [Total Cover](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cover), the sphere discharges lightning at that creature and disappears. That creature makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Lightning damage based on the number of spheres you created, as shown in the following table. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage.

content.label: Shooting Stars
content.text: You can expend 1 to 3 charges as a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action. For every charge you expend, you launch a glowing mote of light from the ring at a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each creature in a 15-foot [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube) originating from that point is showered in sparks and makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 5d4 Radiant damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

This ring stores spells cast into it, holding them until the attuned wearer uses them. The ring can store up to 5 levels worth of spells at a time. When found, it contains 1d6 - 1 levels of stored spells chosen by the DM.

Any creature can cast a spell of level 1 through 5 into the ring by touching the ring as the spell is cast. The spell has no effect other than to be stored in the ring. If the ring can't hold the spell, the spell is expended without effect. The level of the slot used to cast the spell determines how much space it uses.

While wearing this ring, you can cast any spell stored in it. The spell uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell. The spell cast from the ring is no longer stored in it, freeing up space.

While wearing this ring, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws against spells. If you succeed on the save for a spell of level 7 or lower, the spell has no effect on you. If that spell targeted only you and didn't create an area of effect, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to deflect the spell back at the spell's caster; the caster must make a saving throw against the spell using their own spell save DC.
You have a [Swim Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/swim-speed) of 40 feet while wearing this ring.
While wearing this ring, you can cast *[Telekinesis](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/telekinesis)* from it.

This ring has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the ring, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to expend 1 to 3 charges to make a ranged spell attack against one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The ring produces a spectral ram's head and makes its attack roll with a +7 bonus. On a hit, for each charge you spend, the target takes 2d10 Force damage and is pushed 5 feet away from you.

Alternatively, you can expend 1 to 3 of the ring's charges as a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to try to break a nonmagical object you can see within 60 feet of yourself that isn't being worn or carried. The ring makes a Strength check with a +5 bonus for each charge you spend.
While wearing this ring, you can expend 1 of its 3 charges to cast *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* from it. The ring becomes nonmagical when you use the last charge.
If you take Cold damage while wearing this ring, the ring reduces the damage you take by 2d8.
In addition, while wearing this ring, you and everything you wear and carry are unharmed by temperatures of 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower.
While wearing this ring, you cast *[Water Walk](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/water-walk)* from it, targeting only yourself.

While wearing this ring, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to gain X-ray vision with a range of 30 feet for 1 minute. To you, solid objects within that radius appear transparent and don't prevent light from passing through them. The vision can penetrate 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or up to 3 feet of wood or dirt. Thicker substances or a thin sheet of lead block the vision.

Whenever you use the ring again before taking a [Long Rest](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/long-rest), you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 [Exhaustion](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/exhaustion) level.
This robe is adorned with eyelike patterns. While you wear the robe, you gain the following benefits:

items.label: All-Around Vision
items.text: The robe gives you [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Wisdom ([Perception](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/perception)) checks that rely on sight.

items.label: Special Senses
items.text: You have [Darkvision](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/darkvision) and [Truesight](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/truesight), both with a range of 120 feet.

content.label: Drawbacks
content.text: A *[Light](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/light)* spell cast on the robe or a *[Daylight](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/daylight)* spell cast within 5 feet of the robe gives you the [Blinded](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/blinded) condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of your turns, you make a Constitution saving throw (DC 11 for Light or DC 15 for Daylight), ending the condition on yourself on a success.

This robe has 3 charges, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While you wear it, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action and expend 1 charge to cause the garment to display a shifting pattern of dazzling hues until the end of your next turn. During this time, the robe sheds [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 30-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 30 feet, and creatures that can see you have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) on attack rolls against you. Any creature in the [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) that can see you when the robe's power is activated must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the [Stunned](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/stunned) condition until the effect ends.
This black or dark-blue robe is embroidered with small white or silver stars. You gain a +1 bonus to saving throws while you wear it.

Six stars, located on the robe's upper-front portion, are particularly large. While wearing this robe, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to remove one of the stars and expend it to cast the level 5 version of *[Magic Missile](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/magic-missile)*. Daily at dusk, 1d6 removed stars reappear on the robe.

While you wear the robe, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to enter the Astral Plane along with everything you are wearing and carrying. You remain there until you take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to return to the plane you were on. You reappear in the last space you occupied or, if that space is occupied, the nearest unoccupied space.
This elegant garment is made from exquisite cloth and adorned with runes.
You gain these benefits while wearing the robe.

content.label: Armor
content.text: If you aren't wearing armor, your base [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) is 15 plus your Dexterity modifier.

content.label: Magic Resistance
content.text: You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

content.label: War Mage
content.text: Your spell save DC and spell attack bonus each increase by 2.

data.attunement: by a Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard
data.subtitle: Wondrous Item, Legendary (Requires Attunement by a Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard)

content.text: This robe has cloth patches of various shapes and colors covering it. While wearing the robe, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to detach one of the patches, causing it to become the object or creature it represents. Once the last patch is removed, the robe becomes an ordinary garment.
The robe has two of each of the following patches:

items.text: [Bullseye Lantern](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/lantern-bullseye) (filled and lit)
[Dagger](srd-5.2/06/weapons/dagger)
[Mirror](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/mirror)
[Pole](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/pole)
[Rope](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/rope) (coiled)
[Sack](srd-5.2/06/adventuring-gear/sack)

content.text: In addition, the robe has 4d4 other patches. The DM chooses the patches or determines them randomly by rolling on the following table.

rows: Silver coffer (1 foot long, 6 inches wide and deep) worth 500 GP
Iron door (up to 10 feet wide and 10 feet high, barred on one side of your choice), which you can place in an opening you can reach; it conforms to fit the opening, attaching and hinging itself
Open pit (a 10-foot [Cube](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/cube)), which you can place on the ground within 10 feet of yourself
*[Spell Scroll](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/spell-scroll)* containing one spell of level 1, 2, or 3 (your choice)
Window (2 feet by 4 feet, up to 2 feet deep), which you can place on a vertical surface you can reach

content.text: While holding this rod, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to absorb a spell that is targeting only you and doesn't create an area of effect. The absorbed spell's effect is canceled, and the spell's energy—not the spell itself—is stored in the rod. The energy has the same level as the spell when it was cast. A canceled spell dissipates with no effect, and any resources used to cast it are wasted. The rod can absorb and store up to 50 levels of energy over the course of its existence. Once the rod absorbs 50 levels of energy, it can't absorb more. If you are targeted by a spell that the rod can't store, the rod has no effect on that spell.
When you become attuned to the rod, you know how many levels of energy the rod has absorbed over the course of its existence and how many levels of spell energy it currently has stored.

If you are a spellcaster holding the rod, you can convert energy stored in it into spell slots to cast spells you have prepared or know. You can create spell slots only of a level equal to or lower than your own spell slots, up to a maximum of level 5. You use the stored levels in place of your slots but otherwise cast the spell as normal. For example, you can use 3 levels stored in the rod as a level 3 spell slot.
A newly found rod typically has 1d10 levels of spell energy stored in it. A rod that can no longer absorb spell energy and has no energy remaining becomes nonmagical.
This rod has the following properties.

content.label: Alertness
content.text: While holding the rod, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on Wisdom ([Perception](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/perception)) checks and on [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) rolls.

content.label: Spells
content.text: While holding the rod, you can cast the following spells from it:

items.text: *[Detect Evil and Good](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/detect-evil-and-good)*
*[Detect Magic](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/detect-magic)*
*[Detect Poison and Disease](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/detect-poison-and-disease)*
*[See Invisibility](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/see-invisibility)*

content.label: Protective Aura
content.text: As a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action, you can plant the haft end of the rod in the ground, whereupon the rod's head sheds [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 60-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 60 feet. While in that [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light), you and your allies gain a +1 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class) and saving throws and can sense the location of any [Invisible](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/invisible) creature that is also in the [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light).

The rod's head stops glowing and the effect ends after 10 minutes or when a creature takes a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to pull the rod from the ground. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

This rod has a flanged head, and it functions as a magic Mace that grants a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. The rod has properties associated with six different buttons that are set in a row along the haft. It has three other properties as well, detailed below.

content.label: Buttons
content.text: You can press one of the following buttons as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action); a button's effect lasts until you push a different button or until you push the same button again, which causes the rod to revert to its normal form:

items.label: Button 1
items.text: A fiery blade sprouts from the end opposite the rod's flanged head. The flames shed [Bright Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bright-light) in a 40-foot radius and [Dim Light](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/dim-light) for an additional 40 feet, and the blade functions as a magic Longsword or Shortsword (your choice) that deals an extra 2d6 Fire damage on a hit.

items.label: Button 2
items.text: The rod's flanged head folds down and two crescent-shaped blades spring out, transforming the rod into a magic Battleaxe that grants a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it.

items.label: Button 3
items.text: The rod's flanged head folds down, a spear point springs from the rod's tip, and the rod's handle lengthens into a 6-foot haft, transforming the rod into a magic Spear that grants a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it.

items.label: Button 4
items.text: The rod transforms into a climbing pole up to 50 feet long (you specify the length), though the rod's buttons remain within your reach. In surfaces as hard as granite, a spike at the bottom and three hooks at the top anchor the pole. Horizontal bars 3 inches long fold out from the sides, 1 foot apart, forming a ladder. The pole can bear up to 4,000 pounds. More weight or lack of solid anchoring causes the rod to revert to its normal form.

items.label: Button 5
items.text: The rod transforms into a handheld battering ram and grants its user a +10 bonus to Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) checks made to break through doors, barricades, and other barriers.

items.label: Button 6
items.text: The rod assumes or remains in its normal form and indicates magnetic north. (Nothing happens if this function of the rod is used in a location that has no magnetic north.) The rod also gives you knowledge of your approximate depth beneath the ground or your height above it.

content.label: Drain Life
content.text: When you hit a creature with a melee attack using the rod, you can force the target to make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes an extra 4d6 Necrotic damage, and you regain a number of [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) equal to half that Necrotic damage. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

content.label: Paralyze
content.text: When you hit a creature with a melee attack using the rod, you can force the target to make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the [Paralyzed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/paralyzed) condition for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

content.label: Terrify
content.text: While holding the rod, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to force each creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself to make a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a target has the [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) condition for 1 minute. A [Frightened](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/frightened) target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

The rod has 5 charges. While you hold it, you can cast one of the following spells from it: *[Heal](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/heal)* (expends 1 charge) or *[Resurrection](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/resurrection)* (expends 5 charges).
The rod regains 1 expended charge daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the rod disappears in a harmless burst of radiance.

content.text: You can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to present the rod and command obedience from each creature of your choice that you can see within 120 feet of yourself. Each target must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) condition for 8 hours. While [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) in this way, the creature regards you as its trusted leader. If harmed by you or your allies or commanded to do something contrary to its nature, a target ceases to be [Charmed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/charmed) in this way. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

While holding this rod, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to activate it. The rod then instantly transports you and up to 199 other willing creatures you can see to a demiplane. You choose the form the demiplane takes. It could be a tranquil garden, a cheery tavern, an immense palace, a tropical island, a fantastic carnival, or whatever else you can imagine. Regardless of its nature, the demiplane contains enough water and food to sustain its visitors, and the demiplane's environment can't harm its occupants. Everything else that can be interacted with there can exist only there. For example, a flower picked from a garden there disappears if it is taken outside the demiplane.

For each hour spent in the demiplane, a visitor regains [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) as if it had spent 1 [Hit Point Die](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-point-dice). Also, creatures don't age while there, although time passes normally. Visitors can remain there for up to 200 days divided by the number of creatures present (round down).

When the time runs out or you take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to end the effect, all visitors reappear in the location they occupied when you activated the rod or an unoccupied space nearest that location. Once used, this property can't be used again until 10 days have passed.

This 60-foot length of rope can hold up to 3,000 pounds. While holding one end of the rope, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to command the other end of the rope to animate and move toward a destination you choose, up to the rope's length away from you. That end moves 10 feet on your turn when you first command it and 10 feet at the start of each of your subsequent turns until reaching its destination or until you tell it to stop. You can also tell the rope to fasten itself securely to an object or to unfasten itself, to knot or unknot itself, or to coil itself for carrying.

If you tell the rope to knot, large knots appear at 1-foot intervals along the rope. While knotted, the rope shortens to a 50-foot length and grants [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on ability checks made to climb using the rope.

The rope has AC 20, HP 20, and [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to Poison and Psychic damage. It regains 1 [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) every 5 minutes as long as it has at least 1 [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points). If the rope drops to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points), it is destroyed.

This rope is 30 feet long. While holding one end of the rope, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to command the other end to dart forward and entangle one creature you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or have the [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) condition. You can release the target by letting go of your end of the rope (causing the rope to coil up in the target's space) or by using a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to repeat the command (causing the rope to coil up in your hand).

A target [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) by the rope can take an action to make its choice of a DC 15 Strength ([Athletics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/athletics)) or Dexterity ([Acrobatics](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/acrobatics)) check. On a successful check, the target is no longer [Restrained](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/restrained) by the rope. If you're still holding onto the rope when a target escapes from it, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to command the rope to coil up in your hand; otherwise, the rope coils up in the target's space.

The rope has AC 20, HP 20, and [Immunity](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/immunity) to Poison and Psychic damage. It regains 1 [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) every 5 minutes as long as it has at least 1 [Hit Point](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points). If the rope drops to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points), it is destroyed.
This beetle-shaped medallion provides three benefits while it is on your person.

content.label: Defense
content.text: You gain a +1 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class).

content.label: Preservation
content.text: The scarab has 12 charges. If you fail a saving throw against a Necromancy spell or a harmful effect originating from an Undead, you can take a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) to expend 1 charge and turn the failed save into a successful one. The scarab crumbles into powder and is destroyed when its last charge is expended.

content.label: Spell Resistance
content.text: You have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws against spells.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, you can make one attack with it as a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) on each of your turns.

*Sending Stones* come in pairs, with each stone carved to match the other so the pairing is easily recognized. While you touch one stone, you can cast *[Sending](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/sending)* from it. The target is the bearer of the other stone. If no creature bears the other stone, you know that fact as soon as you use the stone, and you don't cast the spell.
Once Sending is cast using either stone, the stones can't be used again until the next dawn. If one of the stones in a pair is destroyed, the other one becomes nonmagical.

While holding this Shield, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) rolls and Wisdom ([Perception](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/perception)) checks. The Shield is emblazoned with a symbol of an eye.
While holding this Shield, you have [Resistance](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/resistance) to damage from attacks made with Ranged weapons.

content.label: Curse
content.text: This Shield is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you are targeted by a *[Remove Curse](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/remove-curse)* spell or similar magic. Removing the Shield fails to end the curse on you. Whenever an attack with a Ranged weapon targets a creature within 10 feet of you, the curse causes you to become the target instead.
While holding this Shield, you have a +2 bonus to [Armor Class](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/armor-class). This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC.
The Shield has the following additional properties that you can use while holding it.

content.label: Forceful Bash
content.text: When you take the [Attack](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/attack) action, you can make one of the attack rolls using the Shield against a target within 5 feet of yourself. Apply your [Proficiency Bonus](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/proficiency) and Strength modifier to the attack roll. On a hit, the Shield deals Force damage to the target equal to 2d6 + 2 plus your Strength modifier, and if the target is a creature, you can push it up to 10 feet directly away from yourself. If the creature is your size or smaller, you can also knock it down, giving it the [Prone](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/prone) condition.

content.label: Protective Field
content.text: As a [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction), when you or an ally you can see within 5 feet of you is targeted by an attack or makes a saving throw against an area of effect, you can use the Shield to create an immobile 5-foot [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) originating from you. When the [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) appears, any creatures or objects not fully contained within it are pushed into the nearest unoccupied spaces outside it. The attack or area of effect that triggered the [Reaction](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/reaction) has no effect on creatures and objects inside the [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation), which lasts as long as you maintain [Concentration](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/concentration), up to 1 minute. Nothing can pass into or out of the [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation). A creature or object inside the [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) can't be damaged by attacks or effects originating from outside, nor can a creature inside the [Emanation](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/emanation) damage anything outside it. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

While you wear these light shoes, you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and along ceilings, while leaving your hands free. You have a [Climb Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/climb-speed) equal to your [Speed](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/speed). However, the slippers don't allow you to move this way on a slippery surface, such as one covered by ice or oil.

This viscous, milky-white substance can form a permanent adhesive bond between any two objects. It must be stored in a jar or flask that has been coated inside with *[Oil of Slipperiness](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/oil-of-slipperiness)*. When found, a container contains 1d6 + 1 ounces.

One ounce of the glue can cover a 1-foot square surface. Applying an ounce of *Sovereign Glue* takes a [Utilize](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/utilize) action, and the applied glue takes 1 minute to set. Once it has done so, the bond it creates can be broken only by the application of *[Universal Solvent](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/universal-solvent)* or *[Oil of Etherealness](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/oil-of-etherealness)*, or with a *[Wish](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/wish)* spell.

A *Spell Scroll* bears the words of a single spell, written in a mystical cipher. If the spell is on your spell list, you can read the scroll and cast its spell without Material components. Otherwise, the scroll is unintelligible. Casting the spell by reading the scroll requires the spell's normal casting time. Once the spell is cast, the scroll crumbles to dust. If the casting is interrupted, the scroll isn't lost.

If the spell is on your spell list but of a higher level than you can normally cast, you make an ability check using your spellcasting ability to determine whether you cast the spell. The DC equals 10 plus the spell's level. On a failed check, the spell disappears from the scroll with no other effect.
The level of the spell on the scroll determines the spell's saving throw DC and attack bonus, as well as the scroll's rarity, as shown in the following table.

content.label: Copying a Scroll into a Spellbook
content.text: A Wizard spell on a *Spell Scroll* can be copied into a spellbook. When a spell is copied in this way, the copier must succeed on an Intelligence (Arcana) check with a DC equal to 10 plus the spell's level. On a successful check, the spell is copied. Whether the check succeeds or fails, the *Spell Scroll* is destroyed.

While holding this Shield, you have [Advantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/advantage) on saving throws against spells and other magical effects, and spell attack rolls have [Disadvantage](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/disadvantage) against you.
This 2-foot-diameter black sphere is a hole in the multiverse, hovering in space and stabilized by a magical field surrounding it.

The sphere obliterates all matter it passes through and all matter that passes through it. Artifacts are the exception. Unless an Artifact is susceptible to damage from a *Sphere of Annihilation*, it passes through the sphere unscathed. Anything else that touches the sphere but isn't wholly engulfed and obliterated by it takes 8d10 Force damage.

content.label: Controlling the Sphere
content.text: A *Sphere of Annihilation* is stationary until someone takes control of it. If you are within 60 feet of a sphere, you can take a [Magic](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/magic) action to make a DC 25 Intelligence ([Arcana](srd-5.2/01/proficiency/skill-proficiencies/skill-list/arcana)) check. On a successful check, you control the sphere until the start of your next turn, and if it was under another creature's control, that creature loses control of the sphere. On a failed check, the sphere moves 10 feet toward you in a straight line.

While in control of the sphere, you can take a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action) to cause it to move in one direction of your choice, up to a number of feet equal to 5 times your Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). Any creature whose space the sphere enters must succeed on a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw or be touched by it, taking 8d10 Force damage. A creature reduced to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points) by this damage is obliterated, leaving its possessions behind but no other physical remains.

content.label: Sphere Interactions
content.text: If the sphere comes into contact with a planar portal (such as that created by the *[Gate](srd-5.2/07/spell-descriptions/gate)* spell) or an extradimensional space (such as that within a *[Portable Hole](srd-5.2/12/magic-items-a-z/portable-hole)*), the DM determines randomly what happens using the following table.

rows: The sphere moves through the portal or into the extradimensional space.
A spatial rift sends the sphere and each creature and object within 180 feet of the sphere to a random plane of existence.

The snake is under your control and shares your [Initiative](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/initiative) count, taking its turn immediately after yours.

On your turn, you can mentally command the snake (no action required) if it is within 60 feet of you and you don't have the [Incapacitated](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/incapacitated) condition. You decide what action the snake takes and where it moves during its turn, or you can issue it a general command, such as to attack your enemies or guard a location. Absent commands from you, the snake defends itself.

As a [Bonus Action](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/bonus-action), you can command the snake to revert to staff form in its current space, and you can't use the staff's property again for 1 hour. If the snake is reduced to 0 [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points), it dies and reverts to its staff form; the staff then shatters and is destroyed. If the snake reverts to staff form before losing all its [Hit Points](srd-5.2/08/rules-definitions/hit-points), it regains all of them.
